8e2bf817dfcfdd84: DALLAS, Sept 11 — Twenty-five years after the September 11, 2001 attacks that would define his presidency, George W. Bush, now an avid painter, is displaying 16 pieces of art inspired by the tragic events.
The exhibit opens with a painting of lower Manhattan shrouded in thick gray smoke under a blue sky, the Twin Towers having both collapsed after being rammed by hijacked passenger jets.

Bush, who had taken office less than eight months earlier, has “returned to this defining moment in American history with brush and canvas, painting the symbols, the people, and the embraces that have stayed with him since,” the exhibit’s introduction says.

It is the latest special collection produced by the 80-year-old former president, who took up painting a few years after leaving office in 2009, with previous exhibits dedicated to portraits of veterans of his post-9/11 wars and American immigrants.

Bush himself is featured in half of the paintings, which include iconic moments, such as when he was informed by staff that a second plane has struck the World Trade Center, and more subtle scenes like him taking the hand of his father, former president George H.W. Bush.
The American flag is a recurring theme in the surprisingly colourful series, displayed at the Bush Presidential Library in Dallas, Texas.

Barely visible in the first painting depicting the attack on Manhattan, the Stars and Stripes are shown filling the entire frame in another illustrating the Pentagon – which was struck by a third plane – and waved by first responders in another.
A visitor looks at paintings by former US President George W. Bush at the George W. Bush Presidential Museum in Dallas, Texas on September 9, 2026. — AFP pic

“These are the moments President Bush chose to paint, because they are the moments he remembers most – not fear, but resolve, not despair, but the instinct of ordinary Americans to come together and help one another,” the exhibit says.
An immense wave of patriotism followed the 9/11 attacks, with American flags displayed throughout the nation, while Bush saw record-high approval ratings.
The commander-in-chief’s poll numbers would later decline dramatically amid widespread opposition to the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and the economic turmoil of the global financial crisis.
“Looking at the paintings I felt like not just remembering all that happened, but remembering that unity that came,” educator Farran Burnette, 40, told AFP after visiting the exhibit.
That the creator of the art was actually president during the events gives them “a different kind of weight,” she said.
“To see it through his eyes in that way is really, really powerful.”
For Anna Catherine Duplantis, a 17-year-old student, Bush’s painting style “really connects you back” to the people and events of the time before she was even born.

“His painting is so raw, there’s not all the structuredness, and it’s not realism. It captures the emotions I think he feels and it can channel those emotions sometimes better than what may look like almost a movie to us,” she said.
In addition to the attacks on New York and the Pentagon in Washington, a fourth hijacked plane crashed in a Pennsylvania field after passengers stormed the cockpit.
Officially 2,977 people were killed in the attacks, with thousands more deaths since linked to 9/11-related illnesses. — AFP
0a13d493fc8c3508: KUALA LUMPUR: Crude palm oil (CPO) prices are expected to trade between RM4,400 and RM4,600 a tonne in the near term, backed by favourable biofuel economics, strengthening El Nino conditions and tighter global vegetable oil supply.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said elevated energy prices had improved biofuel margins, with Indonesian CPO shifting from a premium to gasoil in August 2025 to a discount in August this year.
This is expected to support biodiesel demand and reduce the subsidy burden of Indonesia's B50 biodiesel mandate.

"Meanwhile, unusually dry conditions and low rainfall in Indonesia and Malaysia over the past six weeks, compounded by reduced fertiliser application, raise downside risks to palm oil production from 2027," it said in a note.
The research firm said the forward market was already signalling tighter supply, with palm oil for January to March 2027 trading at a premium of more than RM594 a tonne over October 2026.

"Reduced sunflower oil exports from Russia and Ukraine could also encourage substitution towards palm oil, particularly as Indian refiners typically increase sunflower oil purchases in October-March," it said.
However, elevated Malaysian palm oil inventories could cap near-term gains, with stocks expected to rise another 5.3 per cent month-on-month (MoM) to 2.98 million tonnes in September.

Malaysian palm oil inventories rose 7.5 per cent MoM and 28.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to 2.82 million tonnes in August, exceeding CIMB Securities' forecast of 2.68 million tonnes and consensus expectations of between 2.76 million and 2.78 million tonnes.
The inventory build was mainly due to weaker-than-expected exports, while production rose just 1.4 per cent MoM to 1.82 million tonnes. On a YoY basis, production fell two per cent.
CIMB Securities said exports fell 7.5 per cent MoM and 2.4 per cent YoY to 1.29 million tonnes, likely reflecting weaker demand amid elevated CPO prices.
Domestic disappearance provided some offset, rising 4.8 per cent MoM to 376,000 tonnes, while imports were broadly flat at 49,566 tonnes.
"Overall, the larger-than-expected inventory build reflects a widening imbalance between recovering seasonal production and softer export demand," the firm said.
It said production was likely to remain seasonally firm in the coming months, making a meaningful recovery in exports important to prevent inventories from rising further.
"The higher stock level could cap near-term CPO price upside, although downside may remain cushioned if biological tree stress continues to constrain production growth," it said.
CIMB Securities maintained its 2026 and 2027 CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 and RM4,550 a tonne respectively, as well as its "Overweight" call on the sector.
Its top picks are IOI Corp Bhd, Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd.
5bb617cb9a3b4a75: BEIJING: Twenty-five people died in a fire aboard a foreign cargo vessel undergoing repairs at a state-owned shipyard in the eastern Chinese city of Qingdao on Thursday, state media reported.

The fire broke out at about 11.15am (0315 GMT) at the Qingdao Beihai shipyard during repair and inspection works, state-run Xinhua said. Of the 42 people onboard, 12 were evacuated safely and five were injured and hospitalised.
The blaze was extinguished by early afternoon, state media said.

A picture of the scene released by Xinhua showed the vessel involved to be the Ocean Melody. LSEG ship-tracking data identified it as a 20-year-old Liberia-flagged dry bulk carrier managed by Yuyangkunpeng Shanghai Shp Mgm, with Huili Shipping Co Ltd listed as its registered owner.
The vessel arrived at the Qingdao shipyard on Aug 31 and has remained there since, LSEG data showed.
Chinese President Xi Jinping had called for intensified search-and-rescue efforts, a swift investigation and accountability measures, Xinhua reported.
The shipyard is controlled by state-owned China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC), one of the world's largest shipbuilders.
China CSSC Holdings said in a statement that a fire broke out on a foreign-flagged cargo ship during maintenance work at the shipyard of its Qingdao subsidiary.
CSSC said the company and relevant authorities have mobilised resources to address the situation on-site and all related efforts are under way.
CSSC describes itself as China's principal naval shipbuilder and the country's largest designer and builder of ships and offshore equipment.
A 2022 recruitment notice on the CSSC-owned Qingdao unit's website said the shipyard had annual shipbuilding capacity of 3 million deadweight tons and could repair 212 vessels a year.
e8810643afae9f11: NEW YORK: Top seed Aryna Sabalenka stayed on course for a third consecutive US Open crown on Thursday, storming into the final with a straight sets demolition of American third seed Jessica Pegula.
Sabalenka - who beat Pegula en route to US Open wins in 2024 and 2025 - punched her ticket to Saturday's final with a 7-5, 6-2 win on the Arthur Ashe Stadium court.

The 28-year-old Belarusian, bidding to join Chris Evert and Serena Williams as the only women to win three straight US Open titles, swatted aside Pegula with a dominant service game and a fearsome array of powerful groundstrokes.
Sabalenka will face the winner of Thursday's other semi-final between second seed Elena Rybakina or fourth seed Coco Gauff – who beat Sabalenka in the 2023 final.

On the evidence of her semi-final win, Sabalenka will head into the final bristling with confidence after producing her best performance of the tournament to snuff out Pegula's dream of a first ever Grand Slam title.
"I'm super happy I was able to play such tennis," said Sabalenka, who sent down seven aces and 29 winners. "I was so desperate to win. I wanted it so badly."
Both players gave away little in the first set, serving superbly to keep the match on serve until the 12th game, with Sabalenka leading 6-5.
It was Pegula who would blink first, finding herself down 0-40 after a barrage of hefty groundstrokes from Sabalenka, who clinched the set when Pegula duffed a return into the net.
Sabalenka kept the momentum rolling in the second set, attacking Pegula's suspect second serve and grabbing the crucial break for a 3-1 lead when she lasered a forehand into the corner.
The rest of the set went with serve until the eighth game, when Pegula hit a return long to give up match point.

92f001c5d613a451: MENTION Chow Kit Road and Malaysians will fondly recall the legendary Datuk Sudirman Arshad's massive concert in 1986 which brought people from all walks of life together on the streets in a celebration of Bangsa Malaysia.
Chow Kit is a microcosm of Malaysia where multi-racial folk interact every day as they go about their work — from tailoring to selling street food and sportswear.
Come Sept 18-20, a dance production centred on Chow Kit will premiere at the Jeffrey Cheah Performing Arts Centre in Bandar Sunway, Selangor.

The '3 Days In Chow Kit Road' musical, presented by Kenny Shim Dance Collective (KSDC) and Asia Ballet Academy, reimagines the heart of Kuala Lumpur through an emotionally charged story of love, family and belonging.
In a recent interview, director and choreographer Kenny Shim said the 90-minute story is set over three days in the late 1970s.
"'3 Days In Chow Kit Road' is a fictional story inspired by the atmosphere, culture and community of one of Kuala Lumpur's most iconic neighbourhoods.
"At the heart of the story are Owen, a young delivery boy, and Jasmine, a dressmaking apprentice, whose dreams of building a future together are shattered by an unexpected tragedy.

"'3 Days In Chow Kit Road' explores themes of belonging, prejudice and compassion. As their lives become intertwined with those who inhabit the vibrant markets and hidden nightlife of Chow Kit, the production asks a deep question: is home simply a place we leave behind, or is home found in the people we love?"
The musical features an ensemble of 31 dancers, accompanied by live music and an original score.
Shim explained that the production blends dance, theatre and live music to create a uniquely Malaysian theatrical experience.
"Inspired by the lives of ordinary people, the work celebrates Malaysia's multi-cultural identity through movement and evocative storytelling.
"From the bustling morning markets to the neon-lit nightlife of Chow Kit Road, audiences will experience a richly imagined world where joy, hope and heartbreak coexist."

He added: "'3 Days in Chow Kit Road' places narrative at its centre, using movement as its primary language to tell a story. The production aims to connect with both seasoned theatre-goers and first-time audiences, demonstrating how dance can communicate universal human experiences without the need for words."
'3 Days In Chow Kit Road' stars Hendrick Chee, Amirah Redza, Suhaili Micheline, Lim Sook Meng, Charlotte Phun, James Kan and Mohd Nuriqram.
A STORY BEYOND LABELS
Shim said '3 Days In Chow Kit Road' is inspired by the atmosphere of the iconic borough of Malaysia's capital.
"The idea started with wanting to tell a Malaysian story about ordinary people.
"I became fascinated by Chow Kit in the late 1970s because of its atmosphere, where people from all walks of life, including the marginalised, live as a community."
From there, Shim started imagining the people who might cross paths within different worlds.

"Owen and Jasmine's relationship becomes the heart of the story. Although fictional, I hope the characters feel familiar. They are not historical figures but imagined people who could have belonged to that time and place."
Chow Kit fascinates Shim because it represents many different sides of Kuala Lumpur.

"It has been a place of commerce, migration, nightlife, food, cultures and communities living alongside one another," said Shim, adding that his production is not intended as a historical reconstruction.
"I wanted to look beyond those labels and imagine the human stories behind them. At its heart, this production asks: is home a place, or is it where your heart and family are?"
He added that the main stars come from different backgrounds and experiences.
"I was looking for performers who could bring these characters to life through movement. Dance theatre requires something deeper from just executing choreography well.
"You need performers who understand intention, relationships and character. Sometimes a small glance or hesitation can tell the audience more than a difficult dance sequence."
Shim said music is extremely important because he wants the world of Chow Kit Road to have its own musical identity.
"The production features five musicians and two singers alongside the dancers, and the music has been created specifically for the production.

"Rather than treating music simply as accompaniment, it works together with the choreography to move the story forward and establish the different worlds, from the morning market and romance to the nightlife and darker moments of the story," he explained.
Interestingly, '3 Days In Chow Kit Road' came together very quickly.

Shim said: "It began as a Plan B while another production we had spent almost a year developing was still in negotiation. I had a feeling that I needed an alternative story ready in case things didn't work out. When that project eventually fell through, '3 Days In Chow Kit Road' had to become Plan A."
What surprised Shim was how quickly everyone rallied behind it.

"Within three intensive rehearsal days, we created roughly an hour of material for the first act. That experience reminded me that sometimes creative limitations can force you to make very clear choices."
Shim explained that there are echoes of classic tragic romance and cinematic storytelling in the work, but it isn't an adaptation of any particular film.
"I wanted it to have its own Malaysian identity."
Shim noted that while the timing with Malaysia Day was unintended, he is thrilled the show falls during the national celebrations.
"The timing around Malaysia Day is particularly meaningful because the production celebrates Malaysia without necessarily being a patriotic story in the conventional sense.
"We have a mixed-race wedding, characters from different backgrounds, a shared neighbourhood and people whose lives overlap regardless of race or social status. That, to me, is also Malaysia."
Shim praised the ensemble cast as extraordinary because the nature of the production demands a huge amount of trust.
"I would like to express my gratitude to our collaborators, Asia Ballet Academy and Jeffrey Cheah Performing Arts Centre, for believing in me."
OVERCOMING CONSTRAINTS

On the three intensive rehearsal days, Shim said: "That was probably one of the moments I will cherish most, not because of how much choreography we completed, but because I realised that the company was bigger than any single production.
"There is something very special about watching 31 dancers take ownership of a story and slowly turn fictional characters into people we genuinely care about."
The biggest difficulty has definitely been time.

"We had to rebuild an entire production after plans for our previous project changed. Creating an original narrative, choreography, music, characters and theatrical world within a compressed timeline has been incredibly demanding.
"A new production of this scale needs a theatre capable of supporting not only the dancers, but live musicians, technical design and the visual storytelling we are trying to achieve.
"I'm excited to see how the production transforms once it moves from the rehearsal studio onto the stage."
In the long run, Shim wants to continue creating original Malaysian dance and collaborate with other talent.
"I'm particularly interested in works where dance, theatre, music and Malaysian stories exist together rather than as separate art forms," he said.
THE STORY
The narrative follows Owen, who meets Jasmine while collecting costumes at Miss Lee's dressmaking shop. Drawn to her warmth and optimism, Owen begins to envision a life beyond Chow Kit Road.
As their romance blossoms, another world emerges after sunset.

Jimmy, the feared owner of a popular nightclub, rules through intimidation and violence. Working under his control are sisters Nancy and Maggie, two escorts who have only ever known life within the nightclub's walls.
While Nancy quietly accepts her fate, Maggie longs for freedom and a chance to build a different future.
As the neighbourhood gathers to celebrate a wedding, love and hope briefly unite the community. But resentments, desperate choices and hidden ambition begin to surface.
Tickets for the show at 8.30pm and 3pm are priced from RM58 to RM328.

662d8dabbb7e86e8: SEPTEMBER 11 — This year is the 30th anniversary of the case of Re The Detention of R Sivarasa & Ors [1996].
The facts of the case are straightforward.

On November 9, 1996, 67 people were arrested by the police in an alleged demonstration which took place at Asia Hotel, Kuala Lumpur. The suspects were remanded under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) from November 10 till November 13.

An application was then made in the morning of November 13 to the learned Magistrate for an extension of the detention period of 10 suspects under the same section for another 10 days – that is, November 13 till November 22.
It was indicated in the application that the extension of the detention period had to be made as the period was too short and was insufficient for the police to complete investigation.
In her notes of proceedings, the learned Magistrate stated that she was satisfied with the reasons as appeared in the application, and also in the investigation diary that was given.
Accordingly, the learned Magistrate allowed the application for the extension of detention.

An urgent application was made on the same day at 3.15pm for the order of the learned Magistrate to be revised by the High Court under Section 323 of the CPC. The complaint was that the remand order, made omnibus, on the 10 suspects by the learned Magistrate was not in compliance with Section 117 of the CPC.

That afternoon, High Court Judge K C Vohrah (as he then was), perused the record of proceedings and the documents which the learned Magistrate purported to rely on when she allowed the application, ordering the extension of detention of the 10 suspects.
The learned High Court judge set aside the learned Magistrate’s order, ruling as follows:
(1) The learned magistrate had not appreciated the strict nature of the provisions of Section 117 of the CPC and the case law on the matter.

(2) Pursuant to Section 117 of the CPC, the police officer had a mandatory duty to transmit to a Magistrate a copy of the entries in the diary as prescribed under Section 119 of the CPC when producing a suspect before the Magistrate.

(3) No copy of the entries in the diary was transmitted to the Magistrate. This was fatal to the application for extension of detention, as it meant that the Magistrate did not have the prescribed material to act upon in her judicial enquiry whether to order further remand.

(4) Three sheets of paper were produced before the Magistrate that purportedly contained copies of entries in the investigation as prescribed under Section 119 of the CPC. But they did not. They certainly did not relate to ‘the day by day’ proceedings of the officer making the police investigation which were entered into his diary.

(5) Section 117 of the CPC requires that there be grounds for believing that the accusation or information is well founded for the police officer to make his application for detention. These grounds are subject to judicial scrutiny. It has to be stressed that a Magistrate ought not give a remand order in police custody without satisfying himself or herself as to its necessity and that the period of remand ought also to be restricted to the necessities of the case. If the necessities of the case for remand or further remand are not shown, no remand order should be made.

(6) The liberty of an individual after arrest is at stake and Article 5(4) of the Federal Constitution reposes an onerous judicial duty on a Magistrate to decide whether a person should be detained or detained further.

(7) The application for extension of detention was an omnibus application for the detention of 10 named persons, and there was no condescension to details as to what each of them was arrested for and why it was necessary to extend the remand of each of them. Whatever vague reasons shown on the application (which did not show any nexus between the suspects and a suspected offence or offences) for the continued detention of each of them were without any foundation).

(8) The detention by the police of a person beyond 24 hours after his arrest is not as a result of an executive act but as a result of a judicial decision in consonance with Article 5(4) of the Federal Constitution. It was unfortunate that the Magistrate did not refer to what was required of her under Section 117 of the CPC. She did not appreciate the full import of the section. The order made by her was misconceived.
The case is much celebrated. So too the judge – “a no-nonsense judge, respected by his peers, and before whom lawyers love to appear”.
There was an impression among the police that the remand of a suspect should be done by a Magistrate as a matter of course.
Good riddance to the impression.
It is the duty of the police to comply with the provisions of Sections 117 and 119 of the CPC and that the Magistrate should insist on such strict compliance of the provisions.
If the police do not satisfy the Magistrate that a remand was necessary for the purpose of investigation, the Magistrate should release the suspect.

The learned Magistrate reportedly agreed with Azeez’s lawyers that investigations could proceed without detention.

5d9f1a1f159707ed: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 11 — Domestic violence should not be treated as a private matter or endured alone, as it is a serious form of violence that must not be normalised under any circumstances, said Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying.
She said domestic violence can have a profound impact not only on victims, but also on children, families and the wellbeing of society as a whole.
Lim said efforts to prevent violence, protect victims and ensure they receive the necessary support and access to appropriate assistance must be a shared responsibility.
“To those facing domestic violence, I want to emphasise that you are not alone and that you have the right to seek help and protection,” she said in a Facebook post yesterday.

Lim urged victims to seek immediate help from someone they trust or through appropriate support services, including Talian Kasih at 15999 and WhatsApp at 019-261 5999, which operate round the clock, seven days a week.

She said the ministry will continue to strengthen efforts to prevent violence and provide protection and support to victims and affected families, in line with existing laws and protection mechanisms.
Meanwhile, Lim expressed sadness at the news of the death of Malaysian national Tan Kah Ming in Perth, Australia, last month, which is believed to be linked to domestic violence.

She also conveyed her condolences to the deceased’s family following the tragic loss, saying that the woman’s children and family members will understandably be the focus of attention during this difficult time.

“Regarding the case in Perth, I respect the investigation process and actions taken by the Australian Government. We will leave matters concerning the facts and progress of the investigation to the relevant authorities.
“In this difficult and deeply painful time, let us respect the privacy of Tan’s family and give them the space they need to grieve and come to terms with their loss,” she said.
Tan, 28, from Penang, was reported to have died after allegedly being assaulted late last month.

According to media reports, the mother of three was found unconscious at a residence on Taree Street, St James, at 8.30pm on August 26 before being rushed to Royal Perth Hospital, where she died shortly after arriving. — Bernama
b1053f33e57407e8: SYDNEY: Three-time world sailor of the year Tom Slingsby headlines a powerhouse team unveiled Friday as Australia makes its return to the America's Cup after almost three decades.
Australia will be one of six countries competing for the chance to challenge holders New Zealand in Naples next year for the Auld Mug, first awarded in 1851.
British, Italian, French, Swiss and American teams will also be in contention.
Joining Slingsby are Luke Parkinson, Tash Bryant, Tom Needham, Jason Waterhouse, Sam Newton and Kinley Fowler.
Collectively, the group has four Olympic Games appearances, nine America's Cup campaigns, 24 world championship titles and 13 SailGP titles between them.
It reunites three members of Oracle Team USA's victorious 2013 America's Cup crew — Slingsby, Newton and Fowler.
"We set out to bring together the strongest possible Australian sailing team, and I believe we have done just that," said head of sailing Slingsby.
"We have proven winners alongside some of Australia's most exciting emerging foiling and technical talent.
Each sailor brings a different strength, from racecraft and flight control to engineering, systems and campaign experience."
Australia ended the United States' 132-year dominance of the race in 1983, widely agreed to be the longest winning streak in sporting history, but their last appearance was in 2000.
Next year's America's Cup, the first since the event switched to a two-year cycle, will include a number of innovations including the necessity to have at least one woman in each crew.
The boats will also use battery-powered systems, placing greater emphasis on sailing skill, strategy and flight control.
The Louis Vuitton Cup Challenger Series is in May, with the successful winner progressing to the America's Cup match in July. — AFP

bca7194b63fae956: NEW YORK, Sept 11 — The wife of Venezuela’s deposed leader Nicolas Maduro, both of whom face drug trafficking charges in the United States, has requested to be released from New York detention and placed under house arrest, citing heart problems.

Before her capture by US forces in January, Cilia Flores “was in good health and was not taking any long-term medication, with the exception of a monthly injection,” her attorney Mark Donnelly stated in a document dated Wednesday.

While she and her husband are incarcerated in a federal jail in Brooklyn awaiting trial, the 69-year-old Flores suffers from serious heart problems that require a coronary angiogram or even surgery, according to her defense team.

Arguing that her living conditions in detention do not allow her to receive the proper medical care, the lawyer is requesting she be placed under house arrest in the United States under restrictive conditions, including 24-hour armed surveillance, an electronic ankle bracelet monitor and confiscation of her passport.

The authoritarian Maduro, 63, and Flores were seized by the United States during a raid in Caracas and have been detained since January 3. They stand accused of helping smuggle tons of cocaine into the United States.
Both deny the charges, while Maduro has claimed in court to be a “prisoner of war” of the United States. — AFP
25d7d69db1167b47: PEREIRA, Sept 11 — One month after a powerful earthquake shattered the Colombian city of Pereira, hundreds of people sleep outdoors or seek refuge in shelters with little idea of what the future holds.
Pereira is nestled in Colombia’s western coffee-growing region, which was badly hit by the 7.4 magnitude quake on August 10.
In a park next to the remains of their ruined home, Fanery Andrade and her family have resorted to sleeping in tents alongside similarly displaced households.
Andrade, 41, has not yet seen the much-touted government aid supposedly on its way to people made homeless by the disaster.
“We’re still here because rents are really tough,” the street vendor told AFP.
“We’ve looked around; they’re incredibly expensive. They’ve shot up into the stratosphere,” she said.
The quake brought down schools, hospitals and over 36,300 homes, according to Colombia’s disaster response agency.
Over 330 people were killed, and infrastructure damage is estimated to cost $9.5 billion, while reconstruction will likely take years.
Andrade recalled escaping from her house just moments before it collapsed.
“You still sleep in fear,” she said, gazing at the remains of her home.
Going to a shelter was an option, but Andrade prefers the camaraderie between the six families camped out in the park.
“We all help each other,” she said.
President Abelardo de la Espriella took power three days before the disaster struck.
The right-wing leader has promised to deliver rent subsidies worth US$285 for three months to those who need it.
But several people who qualify for the subsidy told AFP they still have not received the aid.
Francia Elena Vasquez has taken matters into her own hands.
After losing the decades-old family shop selling scented candles and disposable utensils, Vasquez went back to working from a parking lot.
“Thanks to the community, to the people...things have gone well for us,” she said.
Matias Velez lost his home and sustained injuries during the tremor.
The 36-year-old nurse, who wears crutches and has his leg in a cast, is living with his parents while he recovers.
“We have to start from scratch,” he said. — AFP
2ad9eefea83be6e7: NEW DELHI, Sept 11 — Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in the Indian capital today ahead of an 11-member BRICS summit set to be dominated by wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, as well as economic challenges.

Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian were due to hold talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while Chinese President Xi Jinping was also expected to meet him on the sidelines of the two-day meeting, according to Indian diplomatic sources.

Putin arrived at Palam Air Force Station in New Delhi, where he was greeted by India’s Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh, according to footage broadcast by Russia’s Ria Novosti news agency.

For China’s Xi, it will be his first visit to India since 2019 and marks the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the rival neighbours, six years after a deadly military clash along their disputed Himalayan border.
Ties between the nuclear-armed Asian giants have been warming again recently, with flights, visas and high-level contacts gradually being restored.
However, deep mistrust remains, with their contested frontier, a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry still complicating ties.

Posters of a beaming Modi line streets across New Delhi to welcome leaders, with heavy deployments of security forces across the capital and widespread traffic restrictions in central districts. Delhi police have urged people to be patient and cooperative.
BRICS was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers.

It has since expanded and now includes Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates—three countries with sharply differing positions on the war launched by the United States and Israel in February.
“The Gulf conflict is going to be the central fault line this time during the BRICS summit,” said Harsh V. Pant of India’s Observer Research Foundation.
“What was seen until last year as an achievement—the expansion of BRICS—today looks like a big constraint on BRICS,” Pant said.
It will be Pezeshkian’s first visit to India as Iranian president, and will put the Middle East conflict firmly on the agenda.

“The war in Iran will provide a stern test of the (expanded) group’s cohesion,” said Shilan Shah of Capital Economics, noting the failure of the BRICS foreign ministers to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May.
India maintains cordial relations with Iran and Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in its ties with Washington.

India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the Iran war in part by turning to Russia, one of its most important strategic partners and its most controversial fuel supplier in recent years as the war against Ukraine drags on.
Putin last visited India in December 2025, but he also met Modi in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, this month.

Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar visited Kyiv this month, when Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was “grateful to India for its commitment to ending this unjust war”. — AFP

88d2da9eddf652d0: SEPTEMBER 11 — Unknown to possibly many people, particularly Muslims in Malaysia, there appears to be an easier path to Heaven.
The process is quite straightforward. Well, at least according to PAS secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan.
He reportedly said Muslims who joined his party or supported its supposedly Islamic struggles could be on the path to Heaven.
So far, PAS has not dismissed Takiyuddin’s statement as being merely his personal opinion. So, we can only assume that his stand on this serious and controversial matter reflects his party’s.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
PAS secretary‑general Takiyuddin Hassan claimed Muslims who joined his party or backed its Islamic cause were promised a path to Heaven. — Bernama pic

That is why the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan swiftly responded, reminding PAS and people in general that only Allah has the absolute right to determine who deserves a heavenly reward.
He rightly stressed that mere mortals did not have the power to guarantee an easier passage to paradise just because they chose a particular political party or backed its religious struggles.

Takiyuddin’s assertion also prompted a quick response from Amanah vice-president Mahfuz Omar who rightly stressed that certain party affiliation and candidate preference on the ballot paper would not automatically open Heaven’s door.
Instead, he added, a person’s standing before Allah is judged by “faith, piety, good deeds, justice, trustworthiness and the mercy of Allah”. Only God knows and only He decides.
One would add that an expression of humanity, compassion and empathy in daily life is also an important aspect of human character and spirituality.
For instance, one should be able to empathise with, and give comfort to, a mother who pines for her daughter who was snatched away from her ever since she was a toddler.
It would be reasonable to expect that those with the necessary resources would help find the child and make a reunion possible.
Indeed, PAS seemed to think that it, a collective of mere mortals, is fit to intervene in the affairs of the Divine.

Such arrogance does not sit well with humility that Islam often reminds humans of their limitations and failings vis-a-vis Allah’s many attributes, such as the All-Powerful, All-Knowing and the Judge.
At this juncture, one wonders whether the political confidence that the Islamist party has attained in recent times has emboldened it to flaunt its arrogance beyond the material world.
We should be mindful that sometimes there are unintended outcomes arising from such unpleasant behaviour in the real world.

The invitation to join PAS for a ticket to Heaven might attract people you least expect. Certain individuals might rush to join the party soon after being charged with corruption—in the hope that they would not miss the boat, so to speak. Would that make PAS a convenient “spiritual refuge”?

There are also others who might join or remain in the party not solely because of the lure of Heaven. To them, the rewards of becoming party members are two-fold: both the heavenly abode and Putrajaya are seen to be within reach.
It can get complicated, though, when the attraction of the worldly prize overwhelms some members.
The party’s struggles that Takiyuddin mentioned are bound to pique the interests of many people.
For instance, if the unity of the Muslim community (Ummah) is the primary objective of PAS, how would it play out in the wider social context where non-Muslims exist?

Do the struggles also involve a fight against discrimination and racism in our multiethnic, multireligious and multicultural society in the larger objective of creating a cohesive nation? What is at stake here is the notion of diversity and inclusivity.
Would the party’s struggles involve a deep commitment to fighting corruption that has become rampant?

This fight is vital because corruption in our country has brought about precious money lining the pockets of the greedy and powerful, instead of it being poured onto education, healthcare, affordable housing and aid to the needy, to name a few.
In the name of social justice, would the party steadfastly find ways and means to combat poverty and raise the living standards of Malaysians, especially the downtrodden and the marginalised?
Are human rights, such as freedom of expression and the right to dissent, central to the struggles of the party?
These are some of the concerns that may come to mind for many people, which need to be addressed or dealt with adequately.
It’s one thing to promise a heavenly reward, and it’s quite another to ensure a dignified, meaningful and happy life on earth for all, especially the poor and the marginalised.
* This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
382fc988830ea69f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sep 11 — The first time I tried pao fan — a classic Teochew dish of rice submerged in a pork or seafood broth, usually topped with crispy rice — it unlocked something in me.
Growing up, I did enjoy my rice sufficiently lubricated, but submerging it entirely in broth felt a touch too close to congee territory, which I hated. I wanted banjir, not Guantanamo.
Any concerns about rice soaked to a soggy, mushy death in coloured water were immediately quelled by the first mouthful.

My first pao fan, admittedly, was a pretty luxe one: river prawns gave the broth a rich, sweet flavour and a bright orange hue, while the crispy rice gained a brittle, candy-like texture from the plunge.
It left a lasting impression of what pao fan could be.
So when I heard I might find a great one off Jalan Ipoh, off the deep end I went.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The restaurant, which has been around since 1989, sits on the corner of a row of shops in Taman Kok Lian, just off Jalan Ipoh. — Picture by Ethan Lau
I felt a familiar sensation, yet I was arguably more impressed when the pao fan was presented to me at Sun Kar Hee, a 37-year-old Chinese seafood restaurant in Taman Kok Lian, just off Jalan Ipoh.
Situated on the corner of a quiet row of shops, the restaurant is half air-conditioned, half open-air.

The pao fan here is aptly named Seafood Treasure (RM428), justifying its price with quantity as much as quality: crab, white prawns, lala clams, scallop, dried scallops, abalone and thick slices of giant grouper make up the broth's contents, along with cooked rice and crispy rice. It comfortably feeds four to five.

The thing about most brothy seafood dishes like these is that, for all the work that goes into their preparation, it comes down to how good and — though the two are not equivalent — how fresh the seafood is.
And that is where being as established as Sun Kar Hee becomes a real trump card for a seafood restaurant.

Because the crab and lala clams were sweet; the white prawns and great scallop, buoyant and firm; and even with the odd bone, the thick, meaty slices of giant grouper held their structure like well-rested steak.
And the broth delivered a far more subtle, refined sweetness than the first I tried, leaving room for a more savoury, briny character to come through.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Celtuce, also known as ‘wosun’ in Cantonese, stir-fried with wood ear fungus, shimeji mushrooms, carrots and topped with toasted pine nuts. — Picture by Ethan Lau
All of it, dutifully soaked into both the cooked and crispy rice.
You could have a complete meal at Sun Kar Hee.

There’s no shortage of large, banquet-style dishes fit for big groups like claypot drunken chicken and stewed pork trotters with sea cucumber, but my decidedly small group had already begun feeling the effects of our pao fan.

In the interest of balance, we ordered a vegetable dish: stir-fried celtuce (wosun in Cantonese) with wood ear fungus, carrots and white shimeji mushrooms (RM18), fascinatingly topped with toasted pine nuts.
Between the tender crunch of the celtuce and the pop of the pine nuts, the dish made for a wonderful textural experience.

And just because we wanted something to snack on while waiting for the pao fan — the restaurant did inform us that it would take 20 minutes — we also ordered a small portion of cili padi pork belly (RM32), and nibbled on slices of fatty belly in a sweet, sticky sauce with spicy bird’s eye chillies and lots, lots of red onion.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Not bad for a nibble: ‘cili padi’ pork belly. — Picture by Ethan Lau
It has to be said, the rest of the large-format dishes at Sun Kar Hee looked really tempting. I may even consider trying one or two on my next visit.
But I’d have to come with a really, really big group, because there’s no way I’d bring anyone here without letting them try the pao fan.
Sun Kar Hee Restaurant
28, Jalan Manjoi,
Taman Kok Lian, Kuala Lumpur.
Open:11.30am-9.30pm. Closed on Tuesdays.
Facebook: Sun Kar Hee Restaurant

4a4129b19cf613ea: NEW DELHI: India's proposal to put health warning labels on some food products has sparked a nationwide debate over how the country came to rely on cheap packaged food while companies sold more nutritious versions of the same brands in other markets.

With an income per household well below the global average, Indians are keen consumers of cheap food products such as Nestle-owned Maggi instant noodles and Coca-Cola Co's Thums Up — giving big food manufacturers a huge market with little pressure to apply the food standards they adopt in many other countries.
Until now.

In a setback to the industry, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said on Thursday it could introduce tougher red warning labels on ​food that exceeds government-set limits on added sugar, salt or saturated fat in one go, after Supreme Court judges raised questions about FSSAI's initial plan for a phased introduction.
High sugar content is a particular risk in India, which accounts for about a quarter of all global cases of diabetes, which health experts have blamed partly on processed food.
More than 101 million people in India are living with diabetes, while another 136 million have prediabetes, Danish drugmaker Novo Nordisk said in July.
Fast-growing market
India's packaged food market grew to $137.25 billion this year, from $129.18 billion in 2025, and is projected to reach $238.83 billion by 2034, according to research firm IMARC Group.
Around 6 billion meals eaten in Indian households and on street corners every year are Maggi two-minute masala noodles, made by Swiss food giant Nestle.

Maggi launched India's first brand of instant noodles in 1983, targeting newly working mothers and children as a fast evening snack with print ads featuring kids slurping bowls of Maggi noodles "after school, after play" and saying "Mummy, I'm hungry."

The product's success strengthened Nestle's foothold in what is today the company's fastest-growing region, where all variants of Maggi are made with palm ​oil, whereas many versions sold in Britain use pricier sunflower oil.
Similarly, Nestle's KitKat bars in India have less cocoa in them than Australian versions.

"It plays on national pride — why is it that India is getting short-changed? Why do companies make the call on my behalf that I can't afford better ingredients?" said Shashank Mehta, a former marketing manager at Unilever's India unit.
Higher quality ingredients are also more expensive and could prompt price hikes in a cost-conscious market, a former senior Nestle executive, who declined to be named, said.

Nestle said in a statement that its recipes are developed taking into account consumer expectations, local taste preferences depending on the food culture, availability of ingredients and climatic conditions.
Recipe variations do not affect product quality, Nestle said, adding that it has more than 10 regional KitKat recipes globally.
The company said it complies with all Indian food safety laws and that ingredients are clearly declared on packs.
Public anger

India has debated front-of-pack warning labels for years to flag high content of sugar, salt and fat, like those implemented in Chile and Mexico, but faced industry opposition, with businesses specifically worried as many traditional Indian products are high in sugar or fat.
Chile's 2016 food labelling law, which puts separate black octagons on a pack for each high nutrient, was followed by a 23.7 per cent decline in purchases of sugary drinks, researchers have said.
The All India Food Processors' Association says 80 per cent of packaged food could be flagged in India as having high fat, sugar or salt content under the proposed labelling rule.
Pressure in India for stricter labelling has intensified recently from health advocates and social media influencers among others.

The food safety regulator's proposal came amid public anger after Reuters reported that India's government had yielded to industry lobbying in March when Coca-Cola and groups backing Nestle and PepsiCo opposed having warning labels on the front of food and drinks packaging.
Brands never questioned

Western packaged food giants have been in India for about a century. Nestle started to sell sugary condensed milk in 1912 to what was then a British colony with an extremely poor local population. Unilever began selling "dalda" — a hydrogenated vegetable oil formulation — in India in 1937.
It provided a very affordable alternative to expensive traditional ghee and quickly became a staple in lower-class kitchens, restaurants, and sweet shops.
Foreign corporations quickly began producing locally to keep prices low.

"Many recipes in India were designed decades ago for a very cost-conscious consumer, and those recipes have simply been carried forward," said Parul Sharma, a former executive at Mondelez's India unit who oversaw supermarket sales.
"For the longest time, Indian consumers never really questioned brands."
Coca-Cola Co's Thums Up — a cola moulded over decades to suit local tastes — has grown into a more than $1 billion brand that is sold in India and exported to the Indian diaspora.
Thums Up looks similar to Pepsi and Coca Cola but tastes different. Coca-Cola Co bought the brand for about $60 million in 1993 to slowly phase it out and replace it with its own flagship drink.

But Indian shoppers were so loyal to the taste that Coke decided to keep it. Coca-Cola's traditional cola is also a cultural mainstay, sold on street corners with a healthy dose of spices as 'masala coke.'
Coca-Cola did not respond to a request for comment.

A Unilever spokesperson said that in the last five years the company has "made significant progress in reducing both sugar and salt across the portfolio, reflecting our support towards healthier diets."
"We have a long-standing commitment to improving nutrition, guided by rigorous science-based standards."
Former Mondelez executive Sharma said taste entrenchment is one of the biggest deterrents for large companies to modify recipes.
"You can't change a recipe overnight without risking the loss of a very loyal consumer base," Sharma said. — REUTERS

ceeac289bd37b6b9: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — The 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) Asset Recovery Taskforce said claims for damages filed by four companies’ court-appointed liquidators suing DBS Bank are linked to accounts opened by Jho Low associate Eric Tan.

0408eb1355f94b95: BANGKOK: Thailand is considering higher taxes on imported electric vehicles after a surge of low-priced Chinese models intensified competition and put pressure on the country’s vast domestic auto-manufacturing industry.

The national EV policy board agreed in principle Thursday to introduce a three-tier excise-tax structure that would impose the lowest rate on EVs made in Thailand and the highest on fully imported models, Pornchai Thiraveja, excise department chief, said Thursday after a meeting at the finance ministry. An intermediate rate would apply to vehicles relying partly on imported components.

The exact rates for each category have yet to be decided. The board plans to use excise taxes as its sole tool to encourage automakers and suppliers to manufacture in Thailand and increase their use of locally made parts, rewarding companies with deeper domestic production. The proposal will next be submitted to the cabinet for approval.

The shift marks an effort to rebalance a policy that initially used low import barriers to accelerate EV adoption and attract Chinese manufacturers. The influx of imported models has since fueled aggressive price competition, putting pressure on locally produced vehicles and Japanese automakers that have dominated Thailand’s car industry for decades.

Thailand is Southeast Asia’s largest auto-production hub, built on decades of Japanese investment and an extensive network of parts suppliers. The industry accounts for about 3% of gross domestic product, employs more than half a million people and is a major source of exports.

The country is now trying to preserve that manufacturing base through the transition from combustion engines to EVs. Chinese automakers have committed billions of dollars to local factories, but policymakers increasingly want incentives to favor companies that manufacture in the country rather than those relying on imports.
Thailand is also facing growing competition for automotive investment from elsewhere in Southeast Asia. Indonesia and Vietnam are offering incentives to attract new models and factories.

b5f4aa110160d19a: KUALA LUMPUR: That burning sensation after a meal; the bloated feeling that comes and goes; the stomach pain you brush off as "just gastric".

For many Malaysians, it's tempting to pop an over-the-counter antacid and carry on with the day. But doctors warn that recurring symptoms commonly blamed on gastritis could sometimes signal far more serious health conditions, including colorectal cancer, gallstones, pancreatitis, or even a heart attack.
The danger, they say, isn't the discomfort itself - it's assuming you already know what's causing it.
Consultant general and colorectal surgeon Dr Nurhashim Haron said about 40-50% of colorectal cancer patients referred to him initially believed they were simply suffering from gastritis.
"Patients only come for further checks after symptoms persist. As a result, when they are finally diagnosed, more than 70% are already at stage three or four," he told Bernama.
Colorectal cancer is now the second most-common cancer in Malaysia after breast cancer, with national registry data showing cases are rising among both men and women.
More worrying, Nurhashim said, is that patients are also becoming younger. "Previously, most patients were between 55 and 65. Now, we are seeing cases as early as their 40s, and even younger."
One patient in his 40s spent months treating what he believed was "wind" and gastritis with medication from clinics and pharmacies.

An initial upper endoscopy showed only inflammation of the stomach lining. However, a later colonoscopy revealed a tumour in his transverse colon, while a CT scan confirmed the cancer had already reached an advanced stage.
He eventually underwent surgery to remove part of his colon and stomach before beginning chemotherapy.
Nurhashim said people should pay close attention to persistent changes in bowel habits, as these are often among the earliest warning signs of colorectal cancer.

Red flags include blood or mucus in the stool, prolonged diarrhoea or constipation, narrower stools, unexplained changes in bowel frequency, and a persistent feeling that the bowel has not emptied completely.
"Many patients assume these symptoms are caused by gastritis, stress or diet and wait until the condition worsens," he said.
Embarrassment and fear of procedures such as colonoscopies also cause many people to delay seeking medical attention.

Notably, stomach discomfort isn't always linked to the digestive organs. Consultant general and hepatobiliary surgeon Dr Thamarai Velan said gallstones and pancreatitis can also produce symptoms that resemble gastritis.

"Many patients come in complaining of heartburn, indigestion and abdominal discomfort, which they assume is gastritis," he told Bernama. "However, in my experience, more than half of such cases are caused by other conditions."

Unlike gastritis, gallstone pain is often sharper, usually occurs on the right side of the abdomen, and may spread to the back. Some patients also experience nausea, vomiting or yellowing of the eyes and skin if a blocked bile duct causes jaundice.
Thamarai said he is also seeing younger patients with gallstones, a trend he attributes to increasingly sedentary lifestyles, obesity, and diets high in fat but low in fibre.
Left untreated, gallstones can lead to gallbladder infections, pancreatitis or severe infections of the bile ducts that may require intensive care.
Both specialists stressed that recurring digestive symptoms should not be ignored simply because medication provides temporary relief.
"In many cases, symptoms return if the root cause is not identified and treated promptly," Thamarai said.
Nurhashim added that early diagnosis can make all the difference. "When colorectal cancer is detected early, treatment is often simpler, more effective and offers a much better chance of recovery.
"Many patients could be saved if they had come earlier instead of waiting too long."
895e685cc61e8363: PETALING JAYA: Despite leading Umno to convincing victories in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, analysts say the bigger test for party president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will be sustaining the party’s momentum amid mounting controversies and questions over its direction.

Universiti Sains Malaysia’s Sivamurugan Pandian said Zahid remains an asset to Umno due to his firm grip on the party, ability to manage political alliances and success in keeping the Barisan Nasional lynchpin relevant as a key partner in the federal government.
However, he warned that the Bagan Datuk MP's political baggage was piling up.

Sivamurugan said issues that could damage Umno’s image include the recent dispute over spending at Zahid’s rural and regional development ministry, controversies involving Tabung Haji and Felda, as well as the party’s alleged role in an attempt to remove the Negeri Sembilan ruler.
He said it would be unfair to blame Zahid for all three issues since some predated his leadership, but acknowledged that they have nonetheless added to his political baggage.
What has worked in Zahid’s favour, he said, was BN and Umno's performance in the two recent state elections.

He said Zahid has helped Umno bounce back from its poor performance in the 2022 general election and 2025 Sabah state election with strong showings in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, resulting in BN leading both state governments.
“Zahid has brought Umno back into the game, but the challenge is sustaining that momentum.
"Recent controversies risk turning Umno's electoral recovery into an image reversal. The question now is whether he can prevent the baggage from taking Umno backwards,” said Sivamurugan.
Where is Umno heading?
Universiti Putra Malaysia’s Jayum Jawan said Umno’s recent victories may have raised hopes of a comeback but questions remain over where the party is heading.

He pointed out that BN's chosen partner for the next general election (GE16) remains uncertain, with the coalition working with Perikatan Nasional in Negeri Sembilan while still being allies with Pakatan Harapan in the federal government.

Jayum warned that these different positions could leave supporters unsure about Umno’s direction. “He is also seen as lacking clear strategies on how to sustain the blue wave seen in Johor and Negeri Sembilan."
The analyst said Zahid was also faced with the challenge of leading a party still weighed down by controversies involving some of its past and present leaders.
He said allegations of wrongdoing involving Umno figures could dent the party's image among its own supporters, particularly as many had held key positions in institutions now facing scrutiny.
“There is so much about creating bogeymen to put the blame on, but in the final analysis, positions of power in many institutions were previously or presently held by its members."
Syaza Shukri of the International Islamic University Malaysia said Zahid has shown that he remains prepared to defend Umno’s interests despite leading the party into a federal alliance with PH.
However, she said there was still uncertainty over Zahid’s actual stance towards the unity government.
Syaza added that the recent controversies afflicting Umno raise questions about the grand old party's direction following its heavy defeat at the 2022 general election.
“Is Umno reforming itself as promised after the 2022 general election or is it simply ‘business as usual’?” she said.
ab061a0ef46bc685: PETALING JAYA: Walaupun Umno meraih kemenangan pada PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan baru-baru ini, penganalisis beranggapan ujian lebih besar bakal dihadapi Presiden Zahid Hamidi adalah mengekalkan momentum parti di sebalik kontroversi dan persoalan mengenai hala tujunya.

“Zahid mengembalikan kedudukan Umno, namun cabarannya adalah untuk mengekalkan momentum.

Jayum memberi amaran kedudukan berbeza-beza ini mampu membuatkan penyokong keliru berkait hala tujunya.
“Beliau juga dilihat tiada strategi jelas bagaimana mahu mengekalkan gelombang biru yang dilihat di Johor dan Negeri Sembilan,” katanya.

Katanya, dakwaan salah laku melibatkan tokoh Umno mampu menjejaskan imej parti dalam kalangan penyokong sendiri, khususnya kerana ramai yang memegang jawatan penting dalam institusi kini dalam pemerhatian.

Sementara itu, Syaza Shukri dari Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia, berkata Zahid menunjukkan bersedia mempertahankan kepentingan Umno walaupun membawa parti itu dalam kerjasama bersama PH di peringkat persekutuan.

Syaza berkata, kontroversi membelenggu Umno baru-baru ini membangkitkan persoalan mengenai hala tuju parti itu susulan kekalahan teruk dialami pada PRU 2022.
“Adakah Umno melakukan reformasi seperti dijanjikan selepas PRU 2022 atau adakah segalanya sama saja macam biasa?” katanya.
8adbc4d2b25fbd0c: GAZA CITY: The head of the Gaza government media office, Ismail al-Thawabteh, told Anadolu Ajansi on Thursday that 22,000 wounded and sick Palestinians in the Gaza Strip urgently need to travel abroad for treatment.
He wants crossings to be fully opened to allow 1,000 patients to leave daily.
His remarks came in response to Israeli figures on Palestinian movement through Gaza crossings since a ceasefire took effect last October.
The Times of Israel news site earlier cited Israel's Border Crossings Authority, which said around 10,500 people had left Gaza since the ceasefire took effect, according to Anadolu.
The report added that 6,000 returned to Gaza during the period.

"The figures published by the Israeli occupation about the departure of 10,000 Palestinians and the return of 6,000 others since October are very poor and do not meet the minimum level of the catastrophic humanitarian need in the Gaza Strip," said al-Thawabteh.

"The figures are an attempt to beautify the bitter reality in Gaza, where 22,000 wounded and sick people need treatment abroad, including thousands of children whose health conditions are worsening daily," he added.
Al-Thawabteh accused Israel of pursuing a policy of "deliberate procrastination and slow death" against patients by restricting medical evacuations.
He wants the crossings to be fully and immediately opened to ensure the departure of 1,000 wounded and sick people daily to receive needed medical care.
He also urged responding to the demands and rights of around 90,000 Palestinians outside Gaza who are waiting to return to the enclave.

Al-Thawabteh urged the international community, the World Health Organisation (WHO) and UN agencies to exert serious pressure on Israel to stop using the crossings "as a tool of collective punishment," and to ease procedures "away from security complications that cost patients their lives."

"The deliberate drip-feeding policy in the number of travelers contradicts all international and humanitarian laws, and cannot in any way be considered a response to the crushing health and humanitarian crisis facing the strip," he said.
At the end of August, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said thousands of patients in Gaza were still awaiting medical evacuation for urgent treatment.

In a post on X, Tedros said the WHO supported the evacuation of 106 patients, including 19 children, through the Rafah and Kerem Shalom crossings in the last week of August, accompanied by 132 people.
Israel's genocide in Gaza has displaced hundreds of thousands of Palestinians, many of whom have taken shelter in temporary centers and tents across the enclave.

Since Oct. 8, 2023, Israel, with US support, has been carrying out a genocide in Gaza, killing more than 73,000 Palestinians and injuring over 174,000, while destroying around 90 per cent of the enclave's infrastructure. — BERNAMA
6332baa5a4989832: MADRID: Many Real Madrid fans were disappointed when the club extended Vinicius Junior's contract this summer, amid speculation he might depart for Arsenal.
The Brazilian remains one of the key players of the modern Madrid era, having scored the winning goal in the Champions League final in 2022 and netting again as Madrid won the showpiece in 2024.
However, along with superstars Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham, finding balance in a team built around three players who are largely focused on attacking has proven difficult for Los Blancos.
Carlo Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa could not manage it and each left the club over the past two seasons, having failed to win a major trophy since Mbappe's arrival.
Madrid president Florentino Perez, however, has long backed Vinicius.
The winger was his bet when signed at the age of 16 in 2017 and, after helping deliver two Champions League titles, remains a central part of the Madrid chief's plans.
Veteran coach Jose Mourinho was brought back to the Santiago Bernabeu in part to make Madrid's luxury pieces fit together and pull them in line after a chaotic 2025/26 campaign.
The Portuguese coach has acknowledged the difficulty of the task, but believes he can find a solution.
"Tactically, it could be tricky..." admitted Mourinho in August. "(But) they don't play in incompatible positions."
Vinicius has made a promising start statistically but has yet to rediscover the decisive edge that made him one of the most feared forwards in Europe.
Mourinho described him as not yet being at his best after Tuesday's 2-1 Champions League victory over Inter Milan, although he praised the Brazilian's work-rate.
The winger was also whistled by some supporters during the second half before being substituted in the closing stages.
Mourinho walked over to him as he left the pitch and accompanied him towards the bench in a show of support.
"He deserves all my respect. He's not at his best, and we all see that," said Mourinho.
"He's the first to know it and is working very hard to be the Vinicius that decides match after match.
"While not being at his peak, he's working harder than ever, be it in training or in games."
Mourinho recalled the forward's goals against Benfica last season, with Vinicius netting in both legs to eliminate the Portuguese outfit.
"The Vini who is at his best kills games," continued Mourinho.
"Like he killed me in the past when I was with Benfica."
Back on track
The victory over Inter gave Madrid a morale boost after a 1-0 defeat at Real Betis in La Liga last week, their first setback of the season.

They now turn their attention back to the Spanish top flight, where they host Rayo Vallecano on Saturday knowing they cannot afford another slip if they are to keep pace with defending champions Barcelona at the top.
Vinicius has insisted he can play alongside Mbappe and said Mourinho helped convince him there was nowhere better for him to be than Real Madrid.
The coach, meanwhile, has stressed the importance of the forward's willingness to work without the ball.
"When he hasn't been able to defend, it's been due to fatigue, but he put in a very good effort during the game," said Mourinho.
"I have to appreciate that, and I have great respect for the Vini Junior I have encountered.
"The time will come when he decides matches."
That effort was more evident against Inter, when Vinicius made nine recoveries despite not finding joy in attack himself, although his detractors in the Bernabeu did not necessarily appreciate it.
For Mourinho, that work-rate may be enough in the short term while he works at finding the most ruthless version of Vinicius.

524f7f913708e5ed: DALLAS: US Republicans returned to the stage Thursday to close their midterm convention, still betting that Donald Trump's political magnetism can overcome grim election forecasts – while giving Vice President JD Vance a prime-time showcase as a potential heir.
Trump will dominate the finale of the two-day gathering, delivering closing remarks after Vance's keynote address at the American Airlines Centre in downtown Dallas.
The unusual convention has been built around a simple message: Trump may not literally be on November's ballot, but Republicans want the president's supporters to behave as though he is.
That strategy comes with the party under heavy pressure.

US election tracking site Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats will win the House 229-206 and has the Senate on a knife-edge at 50-50. Trump's approval rating has languished in the low-to-mid 30s amid stubborn inflation and an unpopular war with Iran.
Trump dramatically raised the stakes in his opening night keynote Wednesday, promising a US$5,000 "Trump dividend" to every American adult if Republicans retain both chambers of Congress in November.
He also made explicit the convention's central electoral pitch.
"I'm asking you to pretend that I'm on the ballot – I'm on the ballot, I'm on the ballot – just one more time," he said.
He strongly defended the Iran war, predicting victory would bring down oil prices, and warned that the United States would become a "communist country" if Democrats prevail in the election.

Ahead of his Thursday appearance, Trump told Fox News' "The Ingraham Angle" programme that he would act as a bulwark against Democrats' worst instincts if Republicans lost Congress – but added that he was open to dealmaking.
"I'll block all their bad stuff for two years... And probably be able to make deals with them. You know, they're going to want some stuff," he said.
Heir apparent?

As they kicked off the second day, organisers reported that 20,000 spectators had attended the opening day – close to capacity for the arena, which had conspicuous gaps in the crowd during Trump's speech.
Vance's appearance adds intrigue to the closing night.
The 42-year-old vice president is widely regarded as an early front-runner for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, although he has said he will not make a decision until after the midterms.

His place immediately before Trump's closing remarks gives him one of the most prominent speaking slots of the convention and an opportunity to address a party already beginning to consider its post-Trump future.
But in the more immediate contest, Republicans need Vance and other party figures to help deliver Trump's voters in an election in which the president himself is absent from the ballot.
The vice president will reprise the blend of personal biography and populist politics that marked his 2024 convention speech, according to a source familiar with his address.

But he is expected to shift the emphasis from his hardscrabble upbringing and his grandmother to fatherhood, Thursday's first anniversary of the killing of conservative youth activist Charlie Kirk and the country's future.
The convention has resembled an extended Trump rally more than a traditional party meeting, with no nominations or formal business and more than 50 speakers or presentations each night.
The atmosphere inside the arena on Wednesday was festive despite the political headwinds. Yet not all Republicans have embraced the experiment.

Numerous lawmakers in competitive races chose to remain in their districts rather than spend valuable campaign time in Dallas, while both convention nights were facing competition from the opening games of the NFL season.
Those who have shown up will be looking for evidence that Vance can emulate Trump in energizing the voters who powered the flamboyant billionaire's return to the White House.
