117f3a5213ca8265: KUALA LUMPUR: Pasukan Petugas Pemulihan Aset 1MDB memaklumkan tuntutan ganti rugi yang difailkan pelikuidasi lantikan mahkamah bagi empat syarikat yang menyaman DBS Bank adalah berkaitan dengan akaun dibuka sekutu Jho Low, Eric Tan.

Pada Rabu, pelikuidasi empat syarikat, iaitu BlackRock Commodities (Global) Ltd, Platinum Global Luxury Services Ltd, Affinity Equity International Partners, dan TKIL Global Investments Ltd, dilaporkan memfail dan menyerahkan tuntutan ganti rugi melebihi SD1 bilion di Mahkamah Tinggi Singapura ke atas bank pemberi pinjaman terbesar di Asia Tenggara itu.
Dalam kenyataan, pasukan petugas itu memaklumkan berdasarkan penyataan tuntutan difailkan, lima akaun berkenaan telah dibuka dengan DBS, pada 2013.
Menurutnya, dokumen pembukaan akaun untuk empat syarikat itu menamakan Tan Kim Loong, yang lebih dikenali sebagai Eric Tan, sebagai pemilik benefisial tunggal.

Pasukan petugas itu juga turut memaklumkan Tan, yang merupakan penandatangan bagi setiap satu daripada lima akaun berkenaan, ialah warga Malaysia dan sekutu rapat Jho Low yang bertindak sebagai proksinya.

Wang itu, setelah dimasukkan ke dalam lima akaun berkenaan, bukan sekadar disimpan di situ. Ia saling dipindahkan di antara empat syarikat tersebut tanpa sebarang alasan sah, serta dibayar kepada pihak ketiga, termasuk di kedai barangan kemas, penyedia perkhidmatan sewa jet peribadi, dan kelab malam.
Wang itu juga dibayar untuk tujuan pembelian sebuah kapal layar mewah.

"Antara 2013 hingga 2014, lebih daripada USD1 bilion wang yang dicuri daripada 1MDB dan SRC International telah disalurkan melalui keempat-empat syarikat ini. Wang berkenaan adalah milik 1MDB, jadi sebarang pemulihan oleh keempat-empat syarikat dan pelikuidasi lantikan mahkamah merupakan satu pemulihan aset untuk Malaysia," tambah pasukan petugas itu.

Mengalu-alukan tindakan itu, pasukan petugas memaklumkan pelikuidasi yang dilantik oleh mahkamah untuk empat syarikat berkenaan sedang meneruskan tuntutan tersebut demi kepentingan mangsa penipuan, termasuk 1MDB.
Menurutnya, bank merupakan pihak yang berperanan sebagai gatekeeper (penjaga) kepada sistem kewangan.

"Apabila syarikat tidak aktif yang digunakan bagi menyembunyikan aset memindahkan sejumlah wang yang besar secara berulang kali, kemudian digunakan sebagai pembayaran kepada pengedar barangan mewah, sesebuah bank sepatutnya mengemukakan pertanyaan. Namun pertanyaan itu tidak dikemukakan.

"Pendirian kami adalah mudah. Ini merupakan tuntutan yang sewajarnya oleh pelikuidasi lantikan mahkamah dan sebarang wang yang dipulihkan akan dikembalikan kepada rakyat Malaysia," tambah pasukan petugas itu.
080044d7637dcad5: VENICE: A chilling new documentary about Israel's AI-powered mass killing of civilians in Gaza from two Oscar-winning Israeli filmmakers received a 25-minute ovation at its premiere at the Venice Film Festival on Thursday.

The audience clapped continuously for Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor after the screening, an AFP reporter witnessed, setting what is thought to be a new record in Venice after a 23-minute ovation for another film about Gaza last year.
In their film "NAZA", Abraham and Szor used conversations with 24 different Israeli military or intelligence whistleblowers who spoke on condition that their identities be protected.
"We are letting the soldiers and the officers speak about what they did," Abraham told AFP.
"The goal was very simple: we wanted to hear in as much detail as possible, how the systems of killing in Gaza looked like, how they operated," he said.
The 80-minute film left many audience members stunned, with interviewees describing how they felt like they worked in a killing "factory" or a lethal video game.
"NAZA" draws its name from a euphemism used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that are expected to be killed in an airstrike.

It was described as an "urgent, gut-punch" by film magazine Screen, while The Hollywood Reporter said it inspired "outrage...indignity as well. Most certainly disgust, on a profound level, for the current Israeli regime".
Israel's bombardment of Gaza has left around 73,500 Palestinians dead and 174,500 wounded since October 2023, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures the UN deems reliable.
The pounding of the territory followed an attack on Israel by Hamas militants on Oct 7, 2023, that resulted in the death of 1,219 people, according to an AFP tally based on official figures.
First-person testimony
The men and women featured in "NAZA", with their voices and faces digitally altered, detail an AI-powered system known as "Lavender" that was used to identify people for assassination.
"It was done on a mass scale, like a factory," one says, filmed like all of them at night on a roof terrace with an eerily quiet Tel Aviv as the background.

"Lavender" uses data from the mass surveillance of Gaza, where the entire telecommunications network is monitored by Israel, to identify targets based on their phone calls, movements and interactions.
"The systems parameters are so complex, it's hard to understand," one interviewee, who said he worked on the system, told the filmmakers.
Others describe the systematic destruction of civilian homes, the disregard for war and humanitarian laws, and a "general atmosphere" of "hatred" towards Palestinians.
"It's like a video game because everything is done remotely," one interviewee involved in identifying targets says at one point.
Another describes it as "insanely fun".
Gaza films
The result of a nearly three-year investigation, "NAZA" is the only documentary in competition at this year's Venice Film Festival, which wraps up on Saturday.
Ovations can be easily manipulated and are seen as an imperfect measure of a film, but they do give an indication of the impact on festival-goers and critics.
Along with Palestinian peers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, Abraham and Szor won an Oscar in 2025 for their film "No Other Land" about Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank.

Their latest movie has been produced by Britain's Jim Wilson with help from Jonathan Glazer - the team behind Auschwitz-set Oscar winner "The Zone of Interest" - as well as Britain's Guardian newspaper.
The war in Gaza retains broad Israeli public support, but Abraham and Szor said they hoped it would encourage Western nations to drop their backing for Israel and apply pressure through sanctions.

"Those of us inside Israel and Palestine trying to fight for change, need it," Abraham told AFP. "You are weakening the people inside who are supporting human rights and a political solution by refusing to act".
Israel denies deliberately targeting civilians in Gaza, accusing Hamas of hiding among the population of the densely packed and besieged enclave where around two million people lived before the war.

Last year, "The Voice of Hind Rajab", a docu-drama about the killing of a five-year-old Palestinian girl by Israeli forces, picked up second prize at the festival after receiving a 23-minute standing ovation at its premiere.

Increasing numbers of top entertainment figures are openly criticising the Israeli government, as part of a shift in public opinion in Western countries against prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies.
Foreign journalists have been prevented from reporting from Gaza since the start of the conflict, except under tightly controlled conditions with the Israeli military.
991133e182c40eaa: WASHINGTON: Elon Musk's lawyers put the makers of a new four-hour documentary about the multibillionaire on formal legal notice days before its premiere, warning that the film defames him.
The Sept 3 letter from attorney Alex Spiro, addressed to a producer at Alex Gibney's Jigsaw Productions, accuses the Oscar-winning documentarian of building "Musk" around a predetermined conclusion.
It also says Gibney refused to fact-check the film with the world's richest man or the people close to him.
"This project did not begin as an inquiry. It began with a conclusion," Spiro wrote.
The film premiered Tuesday at the Venice Film Festival to a lengthy standing ovation and strong reviews.
Gibney traces the career and life of the South Africa-born Musk from dot-com entrepreneur in Silicon Valley in the early 2000s to becoming the world's first trillionaire.
It also delves into his personal life, including his difficult childhood and the 14 known children he has fathered with a series of women.
Trade bible Variety called it a "lacerating portrait," while Deadline said the "damning" film had "thrashed" Musk as "petty, narcissistic, megalomaniacal, cruel."
The letter puts not only Gibney and Jigsaw on notice but everyone involved in the film's release, including HBO, Bleecker Street and Universal.

It focuses in particular on a sequence that Spiro says advances a conspiracy theory: that Musk knew early on election night 2024 that Trump had won because his Starlink satellites had been used to influence the result.
Jigsaw hit back in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter, saying scrutiny of powerful public figures is protected by the First Amendment.
This was something all Americans should defend, "including the associates of Elon Musk, who has proclaimed himself to be a 'free speech absolutist,'" the statement added.

Gibney's documentaries have often delved into powerful groups, including the Church of Scientology, the Enron corporation and Israel-Iran spy wars in "Zero Days." He won an Academy Award for best documentary for "Taxi to the Dark Side," which tackles the US military's interrogation practices in Afghanistan.

On the grounds that litigation is "reasonably anticipated," the letter from Musk's lawyer orders the filmmakers to preserve every trace of the project, including footage, interview transcripts, research files and internal communications.
Musk has spent several days attacking Gibney on X, the platform he owns, calling the film a "hit piece that misses" and dismissing it as boring.
a7c6389e9d9aa134: NEW YORK: The wife of Venezuela's deposed leader Nicolas Maduro, both of whom face drug trafficking charges in the United States, has requested to be released from New York detention and placed under house arrest, citing heart problems.

Before her capture by US forces in January, Cilia Flores "was in good health and was not taking any long-term medication, with the exception of a monthly injection," her attorney Mark Donnelly stated in a document dated Wednesday.

While she and her husband are incarcerated in a federal jail in Brooklyn awaiting trial, the 69-year-old Flores suffers from serious heart problems that require a coronary angiogram or even surgery, according to her defence team.

Arguing that her living conditions in detention do not allow her to receive the proper medical care, the lawyer is requesting she be placed under house arrest in the United States under restrictive conditions, including 24-hour armed surveillance, an electronic ankle bracelet monitor and confiscation of her passport.

The authoritarian Maduro, 63, and Flores were seized by the United States during a raid in Caracas and have been detained since Jan 3. They stand accused of helping smuggle tonnes of cocaine into the United States.
Both deny the charges, while Maduro has claimed in court to be a "prisoner of war" of the United States.
67e0f76184126c13: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia should move faster to tap India’s economic growth and help Malaysian companies gain a bigger foothold in the market, says an economist.

Yeah Kim Leng of Sunway University said India could become one of Malaysia’s five largest export markets within the next five to 10 years if Malaysia made a concerted effort to deepen its presence there.

Bilateral trade between the two countries hit US$18.6 billion (RM75 billion) last year, making India Malaysia’s 10th largest trading partner. Malaysian exports to India amounted to RM52.3 billion in 2025, up marginally from RM52.13 billion a year earlier.

Yeah likened India’s economic potential today to that of China from the 1980s to the 2010s — a period he refers to as “early China”, when a growing middle class led to a rise in consumer purchasing power.

China has been among Malaysia’s largest trading partners for years now. In 2025, trade between the two countries topped US$191.7 billion (RM541.9 billion). Malaysian exports to China amounted to RM188 billion, up marginally from RM187 billion the year before.

According to the World Bank, India’s economy grew 7.6% in the 2025-26 financial year, making it the fastest-growing major economy, while its population of about 1.5 billion gives businesses access to a vast and increasingly important consumer market.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is expected to meet his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi on Sept 12 and 13. He will then travel to Kerala before returning home on Sept 14.
Malaysia and India have been deepening economic ties since upgrading their relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2024.
Bilateral trade reached US$18.6 billion last year (RM75.2 billion), with Malaysia exporting US$12.2 billion (RM43.9 billion) worth of goods to India.
Yeah told FMT that the opportunities had extended beyond commodities to include semiconductors, artificial intelligence, digital finance, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing.
He said semiconductors offered one of the clearest opportunities for cooperation, with India having strengths in chip design and Malaysia an established assembly, testing and packaging industry.

Malaysian companies should therefore not try to compete with Indian firms on size, he said, but find areas where their engineering skills, technology and experience could fill gaps in India’s growing supply chains.

“The real opportunity is for Malaysian SMEs and mid-cap firms to integrate into India’s expanding supply chains as specialised component suppliers, service providers and technology partners,” he said.
Yeah also said that the success of Anwar’s visit should not be measured simply by the number of memorandums of understanding signed or the value of investment announcements.
Instead, greater attention should be paid to whether Malaysian companies actually secured and delivered contracts in India, and whether initiatives already announced moved forward, he said.

These included plans for closer semiconductor cooperation, a Malaysia-India digital council, cross-border payment links, greater use of ringgit-rupee settlements and proposed cooperation in artificial intelligence.
“The real success indicator will be whether Malaysian companies, especially SMEs, actively enter the Indian market,” Yeah said.
Universiti Malaya international relations expert Geetha Govindasamy said the stronger economic ties showed that both governments were willing to look beyond past disagreements.
These include Malaysia’s criticism of India’s handling of Kashmir and its Citizenship Amendment Act as well as the dispute over India’s request for the extradition of preacher Zakir Naik.
She said Malaysia was valuable to India as a gateway to the wider Asean market, while defence links and Malaysia’s Indian diaspora provided further scope for closer ties.
However, Geetha cautioned against expecting a major breakthrough from Anwar’s meeting with Modi, given that his main purpose in New Delhi would be to attend the BRICS summit.
She said Malaysia could nevertheless deepen its relationship with India without being seen as choosing sides in the broader competition between India and China.
“Strengthening ties with India does not signify choosing New Delhi, nor does maintaining strong relations with China imply siding with Beijing,” she added.
80f88a7a3777bc30: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia perlu bertindak lebih pantas memanfaatkan pertumbuhan ekonomi India dan membantu syarikat tempatan mengukuhkan kedudukan dalam pasaran negara itu, kata seorang ahli ekonomi.

Yeah Kim Leng dari Sunway University berkata India berpotensi menjadi antara lima pasaran eksport terbesar Malaysia dalam tempoh lima hingga 10 tahun akan datang sekiranya usaha bersepadu dilakukan untuk memperluas kehadiran negara di sana.
Perdagangan dua hala antara kedua-dua negara mencecah USD18.6 bilion (RM75 bilion) tahun lalu, menjadikan India rakan dagang ke-10 terbesar Malaysia.
Eksport Malaysia ke India pula bernilai RM52.3 bilion pada 2025, meningkat sedikit berbanding RM52.13 bilion setahun sebelumnya.

Yeah menyamakan potensi ekonomi India ketika ini dengan China dari 1980-an hingga 2010-an, satu tempoh yang disifatkannya sebagai ‘era awal China’, apabila pertumbuhan kelas pertengahan meningkatkan kuasa beli pengguna.

China sudah lama menjadi antara rakan dagang terbesar Malaysia. Pada 2025, perdagangan antara kedua-dua negara melebihi USD191.7 bilion (RM541.9 bilion), manakala eksport Malaysia ke China mencecah RM188 bilion berbanding RM187 bilion tahun sebelumnya.
Menurut Bank Dunia, ekonomi India berkembang 7.6% pada tahun kewangan 2025-26, menjadikannya ekonomi utama yang mencatat pertumbuhan terpantas.
Dengan penduduk kira-kira 1.5 bilion, negara itu juga menawarkan pasaran pengguna yang luas dan semakin penting kepada perniagaan.
Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim dijangka bertemu rakan sejawatannya Narendra Modi di luar Sidang Kemuncak BRICS di New Delhi pada 12 dan 13 Sept.
Beliau kemudian dijadual melawat Kerala sebelum pulang pada 14 Sept.
Malaysia dan India semakin memperkukuh hubungan ekonomi sejak hubungan kedua-dua negara dinaik taraf kepada perkongsian strategik komprehensif pada 2024.
Perdagangan dua hala mencecah USD18.6 bilion (RM75.2 bilion) tahun lalu, dengan Malaysia mengeksport barangan bernilai USD12.2 bilion (RM43.9 bilion) ke India.

Yeah memberitahu FMT, peluang untuk syarikat Malaysia kini tidak lagi terhad kepada komoditi, sebaliknya turut merangkumi semikonduktor, kecerdasan buatan (AI), kewangan digital, tenaga boleh baharu dan pembuatan termaju.

Beliau berkata semikonduktor menawarkan antara peluang kerjasama paling jelas kerana India mempunyai kekuatan dalam reka bentuk cip, manakala Malaysia sudah mempunyai industri pemasangan, pengujian dan pembungkusan yang kukuh.

Menurutnya, syarikat Malaysia tidak seharusnya cuba bersaing dengan syarikat India dari segi saiz, sebaliknya mencari bidang yang membolehkan kemahiran kejuruteraan, teknologi dan pengalaman mereka mengisi jurang dalam rantaian bekalan India yang sedang berkembang.

“Peluang sebenar adalah untuk perusahaan kecil dan sederhana (PKS) serta syarikat bersaiz sederhana Malaysia menjadi sebahagian daripada rantaian bekalan India yang berkembang sebagai pembekal komponen khusus, penyedia perkhidmatan dan rakan teknologi,” katanya.
Yeah juga berkata kejayaan lawatan Anwar tidak seharusnya diukur semata-mata berdasarkan jumlah memorandum persefahaman yang ditandatangani atau nilai pelaburan yang diumumkan.

Sebaliknya, perhatian perlu diberikan kepada sama ada syarikat Malaysia benar-benar berjaya memperoleh serta melaksanakan kontrak di India, selain melihat sama ada inisiatif yang diumumkan sebelum ini menunjukkan kemajuan.

Ini termasuk rancangan mempererat kerjasama semikonduktor, penubuhan majlis digital Malaysia-India, hubungan pembayaran rentas sempadan, penggunaan lebih meluas ringgit dan rupee dalam urus niaga serta cadangan kerjasama dalam AI.
“Petunjuk sebenar kejayaan adalah sama ada syarikat Malaysia, khususnya PKS, benar-benar memasuki pasaran India secara aktif,” kata Yeah.

Pakar hubungan antarabangsa dari Universiti Malaya Geetha Govindasamy berkata hubungan ekonomi yang semakin kukuh menunjukkan kedua-dua kerajaan bersedia mengetepikan perselisihan yang pernah berlaku sebelum ini.
Antaranya kritikan Malaysia terhadap cara India menangani isu Kashmir dan Akta Pindaan Kewarganegaraan, selain pertikaian berkaitan permintaan India supaya pendakwah Dr Zakir Naik diekstradisi.

Beliau berkata Malaysia penting kepada India sebagai pintu masuk ke pasaran Asean yang lebih luas, manakala hubungan pertahanan serta komuniti diaspora India di Malaysia turut membuka ruang untuk hubungan lebih erat.

Bagaimanapun, Geetha mengingatkan supaya tidak terlalu mengharapkan kejayaan besar daripada pertemuan Anwar dengan Modi kerana tujuan utama perdana menteri berada di New Delhi adalah untuk menghadiri Sidang Kemuncak BRICS.
Menurutnya, Malaysia masih boleh memperkukuh hubungan dengan India tanpa dilihat memihak kepada mana-mana negara dalam persaingan lebih luas antara India dan China.
“Memperkukuh hubungan dengan India tidak bermakna Malaysia memilih New Delhi, begitu juga mengekalkan hubungan kukuh dengan China tidak bermaksud kita memihak kepada Beijing,” katanya.
e14c5e3f9567473c: KUALA LUMPUR: Some feelings are difficult to explain, especially when you are sitting across from strangers and being asked to put them into words.

For counsellor K Aahrthi, colour and paper can sometimes make that first step a little easier. She uses Japanese Pastel Nagomi Art as a relaxed way for participants to explore and express what they are feeling.

Also known as the “art of hope”, the approach does not demand advanced drawing skills. Participants work with colour using simple techniques, with the emphasis placed less on producing a perfect picture than on the process itself.

“In Malaysia, therapy and counselling are still perceived as difficult or intimidating by some people,” Aahrthi told Bernama. “So, I use this space to allow them to express their emotions in a relaxed manner.”
She said the activity can help participants reflect on their feelings while becoming more comfortable with sharing them during counselling.

Aahrthi first encountered Pastel Nagomi Art at a workshop and initially imagined using it with her own counselling clients. She later saw potential for taking art therapy beyond the counselling room and into community settings.

One of the first hurdles is often convincing people that they do not need to be artists. “At first, participants tend to be reluctant and say they cannot. But by the end of the session, they usually realise they are capable of creating artwork,” she said.
Some participants, she added, have found that working through colours and images encouraged them to look at themselves from perspectives they had not considered before.
Since 2024, Aahrthi has conducted workshops around the Klang Valley for more than 100 participants, including senior citizens, children and residents of People’s Housing Programme (PPR) communities.
She said she is particularly interested in making these sessions accessible to those who may not otherwise seek out counselling or wellness activities.
Aahrthi also believes there is often a gap between talking about mental health and actually doing something to support it.

“People talk a lot about mental health today, but what matters most is whether they take action. Providing the tools and space to discuss mental health in a community setting is important before someone seeks counselling services," she noted.

Keeping the workshops affordable is another practical challenges. Aahrthi raises funds through the sale of keychains and interactive mental-health tools to help pay for art supplies, allowing some sessions to be offered free or at minimal cost.
She hopes eventually to take the programme beyond the Klang Valley, particularly to more senior citizens and lower-income communities.
For participants such as Khor Jun Yi, the appeal lies in having time to focus inward. The 28-year-old told Bernama that the workshop helped her feel more connected to herself.
Fellow participant S Shankari enjoyed hearing the stories behind other participants’ artwork as well as learning techniques she could continue practising at home.
For the 30-year-old, the session was simple enough to leave her wanting another. “I really enjoyed taking part in the session and hope to join more workshops like this in the future,” she said.
4a8c3f5d35d4eccb: NEW YORK: The wife of Venezuela's deposed leader Nicolas Maduro, both of whom face drug trafficking charges in the US, has requested to be released from New York detention and placed under house arrest, citing heart problems.

Before her capture by US forces in January, Cilia Flores "was in good health and was not taking any long-term medication, with the exception of a monthly injection," her attorney Mark Donnelly stated in a document dated Wednesday.

While she and her husband are incarcerated in a federal jail in Brooklyn awaiting trial, the 69-year-old Flores suffers from serious heart problems that require a coronary angiogram or even surgery, according to her defence team.

Arguing that her living conditions in detention do not allow her to receive the proper medical care, the lawyer is requesting she be placed under house arrest in the US under restrictive conditions, including 24-hour armed surveillance, an electronic ankle bracelet monitor and confiscation of her passport.
The authoritarian Maduro, 63, and Flores were seized by the US during a raid in Caracas and have been detained since Jan 3. They stand accused of helping smuggle tonnes of cocaine into the US.
Both deny the charges, while Maduro has claimed in court to be a "prisoner of war" of the United States.
813cb6a3df6e4d3e: NEW YORK: Princess Diana's famous "revenge dress" that she wore on the evening that then-Prince Charles made a public admission of adultery is to be auctioned in New York in December.
Diana wore the daring off-the-shoulder gown to a gala dinner in London in 1994 on the day that her husband, now the king, admitted during a TV interview to being unfaithful.

"Princess Diana turned the dress into one of the most powerful messages she ever made, during one of the most scrutinized and emotionally charged episodes of her life," said Morgane Halimi of Sotheby's, which announced the upcoming sale on Thursday.
It "gave license to anyone, but especially women, to use fashion beyond adornment and much more intentionally and meaningfully: as a shield, a weapon or both," she said.
The dress, designed by Christina Stambolian, is estimated to fetch between US$150,000 and US$300,000, with some proceeds going to charity.
It was previously auctioned for cancer and AIDS charities in 1997, shortly before Diana died in a car accident in Paris at the age of 36.
977149e1e30f933c: They called him “Einstein” because he was always studying. But he’s otherwise known as Ayyoub Bouaddi.
He’s only 18, from Morocco, and he could just be the signing of the summer.
We’ll see him on Sunday in the 199th Manchester derby. Wearing a City shirt.
They paid £86 million for him, less than the ‘century-plus’ signings of Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez, but a lot for someone of such tender years.
But Bouaddi has always been ahead of his age.
He captained older kids at school, made his European debut three days after his 16th birthday, and helped Lille beat Real Madrid on his 17th.
Now he’s taking a degree in mathematics, he says, “because it enables me to keep my mind alert and understand the game quicker".
City will be hoping he can do the equations amid the blood and thunder of a Manc derby, even if it is off the bench.
He earned rave reviews for his first start in a 2-0 win at Porto on Tuesday so he’s likely to play some part.
United fans are already feeling miffed by his comments on arriving in Manchester last month.
He said: "Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player."
There was a time when the world’s young stars looked up to United, but now, even without Pep Guardiola, City have that status.

Rubbing in the salt, he added: "I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win."
City feel like favourites for the biggest game of the EPL weekend for a variety of reasons.
They have a 100% record, the new boys are bedding in nicely and, not least, they will have enjoyed a huge advantage in preparation.
If 24 hours is a long time in politics, what is 48 in football?
That’s how much longer City have to prepare for Sunday’s game.
Because of the crowded schedule, United drew the short straw of playing their Champions League game last night, whereas City played on Tuesday.
They had to travel, but only to Portugal, and since then have been on the training ground.

With all the data to analyse, recovery time and tactical tweaking to be done, it’s no wonder United boss Michael Carrick admitted that squeezing in a game against Azerbaijani opponents Sabah was “not ideal.”
United’s start has been decidedly mixed, with the shocker of an opening day defeat to Hull City followed by a 5-2 clattering of Ipswich.
Perhaps seeing two promoted sides as the opening fixtures brought an air of complacency to Carrick’s team.
But Everton’s stunning last-minute leveller would surely have removed any that remained.
What is worrying their fans is that United were almost bystanders in an admittedly manic transfer window.
Co-owner Jim Ratcliffe has made it clear they’re not going to pay “silly money”, but if that’s the market rate… you let your rivals get the goodies.
United did spend on midfielders and appear to be focusing on one aspect of the team per season.
Last summer, they strengthened the attack with Benjamin Sesko, Mateus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo.

This season, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Belaba arrived. The fees were enough to make Ratcliffe grit his teeth, if not quite leap off the balcony. But it’s a strange way to fashion a side when the wisdom of generations tells you to build from the back.
And more so when even the ballboys can see where the weaknesses are.
At times, the defence can look like Dad’s Army.
United have the numbers but half of them are either injured or aging, and quantity is no substitute for quality.
The two English stalwarts, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw, are both in their 30s and seem ripe for back-up rather than starting roles this season.
Other experienced defenders, Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt are injured, while the youngsters are still to convince that they can stay fit, let alone be good enough.
Erling Haaland must be licking his lips.
Reports suggest they looked at Lewis Hall and Myles Lewis-Skelly, but the asking prices were not what Ratcliffe was prepared to pay.
In stark and eye-catching contrast, given the charges still hanging over the club, City do not hesitate to pay the big bucks.

But in topping the spending window, they have recruited well. A lot of talent and experience walked out of the Etihad in the summer, but the signs are that ‘The Irreplaceables’ have been astutely replaced.
But given his age and potential, Bouaddi looks like the jewel in the crown.
Although he got a blast from Haaland for not passing to him against Porto, the Norwegian said: “He did a really good game! In training, he’s been amazing. “I told the chairman we’ve got a gem there.”
A telltale sign that his teammates trust him was the confidence they had in passing to him even when he was well-marked. He always got out of trouble.
The French-born son of Moroccan parents may have the shaggy locks and languid look of a typical teenager, but ‘typical’ he’s anything but.
Eschewing social media and video games, he prefers to read books and play chess!
Form goes out of the window in a derby, but you feel he will help City keep United in check on Sunday.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
1251965503978fcd: NEW YORK: Anthropic on Thursday said it had disrupted several allegedly malicious uses of its Claude models over the past eight months, including a suspected Russia-linked cyber espionage campaign and efforts by Chinese AI firms it accused of trying to extract and replicate Claude's capabilities.

Cybercriminals and state-backed hackers were increasingly using AI not just to assist with tasks but to orchestrate and execute large portions of cyberattacks, Anthropic said in its latest Threat Intelligence report.
It added that humans were often overseers rather than hands-on operators.
"The use of AI went beyond simple questions and responses from a chatbot but rather involved the use of multi-agent frameworks executing" tasks, Anthropic said.
Anthropic said it had disrupted attacks from seven China-based labs during that period.
Among the labs Anthropic named were tech giant Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek and Xiaomi.

"Operators it linked to Alibaba ran what Anthropic called the largest "illicit distillation" attack, allegedly aimed at extracting capabilities of Claude models and using them to improve the Chinese tech firm's Qwen models," the company said.
Alibaba did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Anthropic said it observed more than 151 million exchanges it attributed to Alibaba between May and July 2026, peaking at nearly 3 million per day from more than 3,500 accounts it described as fraudulent.
Distillation refers to the process of training smaller AI models using output from larger, more expensive models in a bid to lower the costs of training a new AI tool.

Rather than running bulk queries, Kimi chatbot creator Moonshot and DeepSeek allegedly routed live customer conversations, which sometimes included sensitive information, through Claude and used its responses as training data, Anthropic alleged.

"A hacking group whose tradecraft was consistent with Russia-based threat actor Midnight Blizzard allegedly ran phishing, hotel Wi-Fi hijacking and WhatsApp-takeover operations against targets in the Ukrainian government, military and diplomatic sectors, using AI at nearly every stage," Anthropic said.
The US government has previously linked Midnight Blizzard, a tracking term coined by Microsoft, to Russia's SVR foreign intelligence service.
The Russian Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The group allegedly used AI to build a system that automatically detected when its malware was flagged by security defenses and rewrote the code until it evaded detection again.

Anthropic also identified what it called "new categories of threat actors" misusing Claude, including those using the platform to "develop software for conventional weapons, including firearms, missiles, armed drones, bombs, and other munitions, as well as the targeting and control systems that operate them".

The report detailed incidents of operators using Claude to develop software for weapons design and development, or to support intelligence gathering and procurement related to weapons programs, in China, Russia, and Yemen.

The company said that it detected and disrupted activity linked to affiliates of the ShinyHunters cybercrime collective, one of the most prolific cybercrime enterprises in recent months linked to attacks on major corporations around the world.
Jacob Klein, head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, said in an interview that models have become more capable over the last year, raising new risks.
"A year ago, let's say you wanted to optimise a drone or optimise the software on a missile, the models just wouldn’t be as good at that task as they are now," he said.
de2610db8c21c4c2: WASHINGTON: Elon Musk's lawyers put the makers of a new four-hour documentary about the multibillionaire on formal legal notice days before its premiere, warning that the film defames him.
The Sept 3 letter from attorney Alex Spiro, addressed to a producer at Alex Gibney's Jigsaw Productions, accuses the Oscar-winning documentarian of building "Musk" around a predetermined conclusion.
It also says Gibney refused to fact-check the film with the world's richest man or the people close to him.
"This project did not begin as an inquiry. It began with a conclusion," Spiro wrote.
The film premiered Tuesday at the Venice Film Festival to a lengthy standing ovation and strong reviews.
Gibney traces the career and life of the South Africa-born Musk from dot-com entrepreneur in Silicon Valley in the early 2000s to becoming the world's first trillionaire.
It also delves into his personal life, including his difficult childhood and the 14 known children he has fathered with a series of women.
Trade bible Variety called it a "lacerating portrait", while Deadline said the "damning" film had "thrashed" Musk as "petty, narcissistic, megalomaniacal, cruel."
The letter puts not only Gibney and Jigsaw on notice but everyone involved in the film's release, including HBO, Bleecker Street and Universal.

It focuses in particular on a sequence that Spiro says advances a conspiracy theory: that Musk knew early on election night 2024 that Trump had won because his Starlink satellites had been used to influence the result.
Jigsaw hit back in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter, saying scrutiny of powerful public figures is protected by the First Amendment.
This was something all Americans should defend, "including the associates of Elon Musk, who has proclaimed himself to be a 'free speech absolutist,'" the statement added.

Gibney's documentaries have often delved into powerful groups, including the Church of Scientology, the Enron corporation and Israel-Iran spy wars in "Zero Days". He won an Academy Award for best documentary for "Taxi to the Dark Side", which tackles the US military's interrogation practices in Afghanistan.

On the grounds that litigation is "reasonably anticipated", the letter from Musk's lawyer orders the filmmakers to preserve every trace of the project, including footage, interview transcripts, research files and internal communications.
Musk has spent several days attacking Gibney on X, the platform he owns, calling the film a "hit piece that misses" and dismissing it as boring.
5dda3799ac351822: WASHINGTON: The Trump administration has proposed eliminating a 60-day grace period that allows certain immigrants, including skilled workers on H-1B visas, to stay in the United States and find a new sponsor after losing their job, according to a government notice posted online Thursday.

Under the planned rule change, published in the Federal Register by the US Department of Homeland Security, those with H-1B and certain other temporary work visas would have to leave the country as soon as their employment ends — a potential blow to top American tech companies that rely heavily on foreign workers.

It is the latest step by US President Donald Trump to limit legal migration since returning to office in January 2025. His administration has also introduced higher visa fees for skilled workers and recently paused immigrant visa appointments at US missions around the world while it implements a new training programme.

Companies impacted by the change could see some disruption, DHS wrote in its proposal, but it said the jobs could go to American workers instead. In some situations, immigrant workers who leave could potentially reapply if their employer petitions for them, it added.
"DHS presumes that they will either offer the same jobs to equally qualified US workers or go through the I-129 petition process depending on their workforce requirement," the notice said.

The 60-day grace period, in place since 2017, allows foreign workers time to find another US job or get their affairs in order — whether selling a home or pulling children out of school — before leaving the country.

H-1B visas, established by Congress in 1990, are especially critical for tech companies seeking talent from India and China, allowing them to fill roles where there is sometimes a lack of qualified US workers.

Consultancy companies such as Deloitte, PwC and Ernst & Young as well as outsourcing giants like Tata Consultancy Services TCS.NS, Infosys INFY.NS, HCL Tech HCLT.NS and LTIMindtree LTIM.NS are top H-1B sponsors.

Lawyers for Berardi Immigration Law, which specialises in business-related immigration issues, said the move would "sharply compress the timeline HR teams have to manage layoffs and offboarding for foreign national employees."

If implemented, the change would also apply to E-1 international trader visa holders; E-2 commercial vehicle operator visa holders; L-1 short-term work for executives or managers with international companies; O-1 visas for people "with an extraordinary ability" in science, sports or the arts; and TN professional workers.
It also would impact H-1B1 skilled worker visa holders from Singapore and Chile and E-3 specialty worker visa holders from Australia.
The rule is subject to a two-month public comment period before it can be enacted into law.
371ca8c99339e1ed: In an exclusive interview with Media Prima, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi tells ADIB POVERA and IYLIA MARSYA ISKANDAR that Umno's push for Malay unity must not be mistaken as a form of narrow identity politics
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno is preparing for the 16th General Election (GE16) with a renewed focus on strategic political cooperation, centrist politics and rebuilding its appeal among middle-ground voters.

As the party charts its way forward, president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has also sought to distinguish Umno's emphasis on Malay unity from what critics have described as identity politics, stressing that the party recognises Malaysia's multiracial character.

With efforts to bring back former members and leaders through the Rumah Bangsa initiative, Zahid said Umno remained open to those seeking to return, while Barisan Nasional was also widening its membership to those who wanted to join the coalition directly.

In an exclusive interview with Media Prima Bhd amid the Umno general assembly, Zahid outlined Umno's approach to GE16, its evolving political partnerships and efforts to remain relevant as it looks towards the next decade.
Question: What are the main messages Umno wants to convey at the general assembly, particularly with GE16 approaching?

Answer: There are three aspects that I believe will be the key takeaways for delegates. Firstly, the question of what form of cooperation we will pursue. We know there won't be a situation where we contest entirely on our own and face three- or four-cornered fights.
This time, we will certainly be looking for strategic friends and partners to face GE16.
Second is how we should formulate agendas concerning the Malays, Muslims and the wider population for at least the next decade.
Thirdly, we (Umno) are already in our 80s. As we approach the next decade, people will ask whether Umno remains relevant.
But we can look at countries where political parties have existed for even longer than Umno and have succeeded in dominating governments or returning to power after losing it.
These three aspects will serve as a guide for delegates to reflect on after the assembly and put them into practice as part of the party's next agenda.
Q: The mood at the assembly is expected to be lively, especially following Umno and Barisan Nasional's recent successes in the state elections. What issues do you expect to take centre stage?

A: Most importantly, we do not want internal problems. At the same time, we cannot avoid discussing issues raised by the states, including providing clarification and responding to the congresses, conventions and assemblies held by other political parties. We are not being defensive. We want to correct the negative perceptions levelled against Umno and BN.

There are various ways of doing this, including through persuasion. We do not want to take an approach of attacking those who have made inappropriate remarks, even though some of them are our political partners.
Q: In the past two state elections, Umno and BN have consistently shared their aspirations rather than attacking political rivals. Why maintain this approach?
A: We're a consistent party. We've always been moderate. We don't want to move too far to the left or right. We take the middle path to safeguard the interests of all parties.

Malaysia is a multiracial country with people from various backgrounds, and we deeply respect that reality. This approach is better than other approaches, whether it is excessive praise or attacking others. We avoid both.
Q: Some Pakatan Harapan leaders have portrayed identity politics in a negative light. Does Umno see itself as a party that promotes identity politics?

A: Whatever optics people want to portray and whatever narrative they want to create, it is the voters who make the assessment. The question is whether an issue that is raised will increase or reduce votes. We are taking an approach aimed at gaining votes from what used to be called the middle-ground, or those with a high degree of political rationality.
That is where we are heading, rather than taking a highly adverse or antagonistic approach.
Q: Do you think Umno-BN's emphasis on Malay unity during the recent elections was misunderstood as identity politics that could frighten non-Malays? What will Umno do to correct this narrative?

A: The situation has changed. People have come to realise that over the past eight years, that assessment was wrong. They no longer see Umno as being extremely right-wing or left-wing. We have always taken the middle path, although there have continued to be misinterpretations.

Those in the government, in particular, may try to portray it in different ways. But for us, what we do reflects what's in our minds. We want to show that the sincerity of what we have been doing will bear fruit. This was proven by what happened in Johor and Negri Sembilan. We hope the same will happen in Melaka.

The grassroots certainly want unity among the Malays. We regard this as a priority in shaping the future of our politics. However, we must also acknowledge the reality that Malaysia's multiracial character must serve as the foundation as we navigate an increasingly complex political landscape over the coming decade.
Q: Issues surrounding the Royal Commission of Inquiry on Tabung Haji and the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) appear to be framed as narratives against Umno. How does the party view this?

A: The same strategy has been used by previous leaderships, but it hasn't succeeded in changing people's minds because support is already deeply rooted in their hearts. Moreover, today's target groups are different from previous generations.

They're not just interested in issues but also in the agenda we will implement. History has shown that what worked in the past may not necessarily be suitable for the generation that will shape perceptions and thinking in the future.
We believe the people know who they want to support. Perceptions can be created, but they cannot win over the hearts and minds of the people we are trying to reach.
Q: Since the introduction of the Rumah Bangsa initiative, how would you describe Umno's relationship with the other BN component parties?
A: Within Umno, we can see the results of Rumah Bangsa and the number of people who have returned to the party.

For BN, we also have direct membership. There may be people who want to join BN but are not interested in joining any of the component parties or parties that are friends of BN. They may prefer to become direct members of BN.
So, we are opening our doors widely to those who want to be with Umno through Rumah Bangsa, as well as those who want to join BN directly.
Q: There have been calls for former leaders, including Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, to return to Umno through Rumah Bangsa. How do you view this?

A: We are always open to accepting those who may have gone astray previously or had very different perceptions. They may develop a new awareness that Umno remains on the right track, even if some of them had previously called for the party to be dissolved.
For the current Umno leadership, we are prepared to accept anyone who wants to return, as long as they do not have a hidden agenda to destroy Umno from within.
Q: Between PH and Perikatan Nasional, which would be more attractive to BN and Umno as a political partner?
A: We look at the manfaat, or benefits, and mudarat, or disadvantages. In Johor, we were using the same approach, but we were prepared to go solo because the political landscape there required it.

In Negri Sembilan, however, we believed there were greater benefits in working with one of the other coalitions. So, we assess the benefits and disadvantages through what we call a political balance sheet for each state.
We then look at the political profit-and-loss account. Are we in the black or in the red? Are we within the bracket or outside it?
We look at the political returns that we can gain, and this will determine whether negotiations can be undertaken by the leadership of the state concerned.

Q: Political observers have claimed that relations between Umno and several parties in the unity government have recently become strained, especially after the past two state elections. What is your view on this?
A: Umno is very pragmatic. Critics previously coined the term "UMDAP" to describe Umno. However, that term is no longer being used in relation to the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections.
We do not hate any political party because we know their character, as well as that of anyone who is either our political rival or our friend.
So, we look at the political wave. If the blue wave is taking place, then that is the blue wave we will bring to the states where we will contest state or general elections.

d89af99baedec961: GENEVA: Several people were killed and injured when a coach carrying Dutch tourists in eastern Switzerland crashed, police said on Thursday.
The accident happened at about 4.45 pm between the communes of Susch and Zernez in the far-eastern canton of Graubunden.
The coach hit a safety barrier before overturning and plunging down an embankment, a local police spokesman told Swiss media.
The Dutch Federation of Travel Agencies (ANVR) told AFP that the coach belonged to the tour company Oad and was carrying 48 passengers, all of them from the Netherlands.

"Several people died in the coach crash in Susch. Several others were also injured," the cantonal police said on X, without giving details on the circumstances of the accident or the victims' identities.
A police spokesman told AFP that the force did not wish to provide a more detailed toll until the victims' families had been informed.
According to the ANVR, the coach left the Netherlands on Monday and was on a day trip to Switzerland from Austria when the crash happened.
Footage broadcast by Swiss media showed many rescue workers rushing about around the coach and helicopters stationed nearby.
Oad said in a statement it was "deeply shocked and devastated by the tragic accident".

"Our thoughts are with everyone involved and their loved ones. Local authorities are currently fully engaged in relief efforts and in determining the situation and the number of casualties," it added.
"We are doing everything in our power to obtain clarity quickly and to support those involved and their families wherever possible."
Swiss President Guy Parmelin offered his condolences to the families of the victims, calling the crash a "tragic accident".
Zernez is the entry point for visitors to the Swiss national park, a vast Alpine reserve stretching more than 100 square kilometres across the mountainous Engadine valley.
57cba654101c9172: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming part of everyday life, from how people search for information and communicate to how businesses serve their customers.
Now, the government wants to take that further, aiming to make Malaysia an “AI nation” by 2030.
What does that actually mean for Malaysians in their daily lives?
National AI Action Plan 2026 to 2030
The National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 is the government’s roadmap for increasing the responsible adoption and development of AI.
By 2030, the government wants AI to contribute an additional 1.2 percentage points to GDP growth and place Malaysia among the top 10 countries globally in the Global AI Index.
It also aims to create 300,000 jobs attributable to AI by 2030.
Changes that have taken place
One of the most visible changes could be how Malaysians deal with the government.
The plan calls for an AI-augmented civil service, using AI to improve public-service delivery and administrative efficiency.
MyGOV Malaysia is an early example.

As of July 2026, it had more than 2.9 million users and offered 52 services from 19 government agencies, including MyJPJ, MySejahtera, PriceCatcher, Portal Manfaat, Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and immigration-related services.
The government is now testing agentic AI on MyGOV.
Unlike a conventional chatbot, agentic AI can understand what a user wants, identify the relevant service and, where authorised, help carry out the required steps.
The government has cited checking a police summons and proceeding to payment as an example.
The rollout is being phased in, with data privacy, security, accuracy and human oversight among the government’s considerations.
What has AI incorporation so far
The examples of government services that have incorporated AI include:
MyJPJ — driving and vehicle services
MySejahtera — health services
PriceCatcher — consumer price information
Portal Manfaat — government assistance information
STR — cash aid-related services
MySPR Semak — election information
Immigration — passport and immigration services
Examination services — examination results
The Ministry of Digital has confirmed the 19 participating agencies but has not published a complete agency-by-agency list in its latest announcement.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo has described Malaysia’s AI push as a “whole-of-nation” approach, involving government, industry, academia and the public.
Jobs will change
The government is looking at creating 300,000 AI-attributable jobs by 2030, although it has not published a breakdown by occupation.

TalentCorp has identified emerging roles including AI engineers, AI and machine-learning application engineers, AI integration engineers, data scientists, data engineers, AI auditors and AI ethicists.
Its study covers 949 roles across 10 sectors, including electrical and electronics, aerospace, energy and power, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, global business services, ICT and retail.
The government is also targeting 700,000 workers for reskilling under its Malaysia Digital 2030 Action Plan, through programmes such as Jelajah AI MyMahir.
No need to panic, try to adapt
AI is expected to change the way Malaysians work, but the government’s approach is not simply about replacing workers with machines.
TalentCorp has warned that hundreds of thousands of Malaysian workers could be significantly affected by technological changes if reskilling and upskilling are not intensified.
Its response includes programmes such as Jelajah AI MyMahir, which provides practical AI training to different groups.
In other words, the message is less “AI will take your job” and more “your job may change, so learn how to work with AI”.
In line with this, the government has set a target to transform 80 per cent of the population to be digitally literate by 2030.
Free AI education
The government is already providing free digital and AI courses through Rakyat Digital, covering areas such as generative AI, cybersecurity and cloud technology.
Under AI Untuk Rakyat, the government is targeting 100,000 Malaysian youths aged 18 to 30 through 2027, with the programme rolling out in phases from August 31, 2026.
Those who complete and pass all required modules will receive a free three-month subscription to a suite of selected AI applications and software.
Beyond jobs and government services
The government is also working to expand AI adoption in healthcare, education, transportation, agriculture and small businesses.
That could mean AI supporting personalised learning, helping healthcare professionals, improving agricultural monitoring or assisting small businesses with routine tasks.
At the same time, the government is putting greater emphasis on AI safety and responsible use.

AI Malaysia Berhad, established on July 28, 2026, is the country’s national AI agency, with responsibilities that include AI policy, implementation of the national AI agenda, governance, capability development and the Malaysia AI Safety Institute.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has said organisations adopting AI should do so responsibly, transparently and ethically, while consumers need confidence that their data is protected.
What does becoming an AI nation mean for Malaysians?
For most people, it does not mean receiving a new government benefit simply because Malaysia has an AI strategy.
It means AI is expected to become increasingly embedded in government services, workplaces, education and businesses.
It is about preparing Malaysians for a country where AI plays a much larger role in how people work, learn and access services.
4dc7fa682832f2ee: BANGKOK, Sept 11 — Nawee Changpirom has spent years working to rescue trafficked wildlife in Thailand, but even he can sometimes hardly believe the creatures he has found: leopards, hornbills, and once an anteater.
“We even found living corals hidden in a ceiling,” he told AFP.

Nawee heads a raid unit in the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation (DNP) that tries to stop the sale of everything from African elephant ivory to monkeys wanted as pets or for laboratory testing.
Alongside weapons, drugs and human trafficking, the illegal wildlife trade is among the most widespread and profitable forms of organised crime globally, run by cross-border cartels.
Thailand occupies a rare position because of its abundant local wildlife, the availability of rare species in nearby countries, and its accessibility by sea, air and land.
The DNP set up a dedicated Wildlife Crime Intelligence Unit (WCU) in 2023 with three permanent staff charged with tracking and intercepting illegal purchases.
They spend much of their time trawling social media, which is now “the key channel” for buying and selling illegal animals, said WCU director Polawee Buchakiet.
Wildlife traders often describe animals as needing to be “rehomed”, rather than explicitly offering them for sale, and post tightly cropped images of their wares to avoid revealing their locations.
But the WCU has undercover officers who can track them down.
Undercover officers

One undercover officer – known by the pseudonym “Tee” – has shinned up electricity poles disguised as a repairman to peer into courtyards and take photos, and posed as a land surveyor to look into windows on neighbouring plots.
The WCU needs such evidence to obtain court warrants to go in and seize the animals.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A hornbill was intercepted by the Wildlife Crime Intelligence Unit at the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation in Bangkok. — AFP pic
He is still haunted by cases where sellers could not be located, or the team arrived too late, finding the creatures either dead or so sickly they died soon after rescue.
Trafficked animals are often weakened by the process of smuggling, stressed by the loss of their habitat and family group, and vulnerable to unfamiliar diseases.
“I wonder to myself if we could have done something to get there sooner,” Tee, 43, told AFP.
“Whether they are big or small, all animals’ lives are precious.”
Exotic pets
At just six months old, the leaf monkey curled up inside DNP vet Thanawadee Phaichana’s rubber-gloved hand is very small indeed.
He was intercepted in luggage at Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi Airport, bound for India, where demand for exotic animals as pets has been growing.
A second monkey found in the same bag died after being rescued.
“Most of these smuggled animals will be in a weak condition... some are given sedatives or even mild anesthetic to keep them from moving or making noise,” Thanawadee said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A six-month-old leaf monkey was intercepted at Suvarnabhumi Airport while being smuggled to India, in the hands of veterinarian Thanawadee Phaichana at the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation headquarters in Bangkok. — AFP pic
Animals rescued in and around Bangkok often come to the DNP’s small facility for initial treatment before being transferred to a sanctuary.
Older, healthier animals might eventually return to the wild, but younger ones struggle to learn the skills needed to survive.
“I feel sorry for them,” said Thanawadee.
Wildlife traffickers can face up to 10 years in prison for crimes involving protected species, or 15 years for endangered species.
There has been a string of recent high-profile arrests, including a July raid that rescued a leaf monkey, a gibbon and hundreds of turtles, as well as multiple interceptions at airports.
But there have also been setbacks.
In 2019, a Thai court dismissed the case against suspected wildlife trafficking kingpin Boonchai Bach. While the Supreme Court later sentenced him to prison, he remains at large.
The team also struggles with stonewalling from social media sites and chronic shortages of staff and funds.
Officers posing as undercover buyers sometimes have to use their own money, Nawee said.
What would make a real difference? An end to the exotic pet trade, he said.
“These are wild animals, they don’t belong in a cage.” — AFP
eb69fcf553644b09: LONDON, Sept 11 — London’s sold-out Bayeux Tapestry exhibition will open Thursday to a British public gripped by “mania” as the medieval artwork depicting the Norman conquest of England goes on display outside France for the first time.

The British Museum will open its doors after months of growing anticipation, heightened by the tapestry’s high-security July arrival in London and last week’s royal preview for the king and queen alongside French President Emmanuel Macron.
The unprecedented loan from France, the result of years of diplomacy and set to last until next July, has been hailed a symbol of renewed cross-Channel ties following the rancour of Brexit.

Long online queues formed for the first tranche of tickets released on July 1, which were snapped up within hours. The British Museum has so far sold a record 100,000 tickets, which cost £25-£33 (RM138-RM182) for adults.
The Times newspaper called the exhibition a “spine-shivering experience” that has sparked “Tapestry-mania” in Britain, while The Economist dubbed it the “hottest ticket” around.
Depicting the 1066 Battle of Hastings and the invasion by William the Conqueror’s Norman army, the tapestry has shadowy origins.
It is widely thought to have been made in England almost 1,000 years ago before being transferred to Bayeux in France.
‘Symbol of trust’
Many in the UK see the loan as the tapestry coming home, with Prime Minister Andy Burnham having called it a “return”.
King Charles III said the temporary transfer was a “a precious symbol of trust at a time when trust seems sadly to be in short supply between nations”.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

People lean over the display case to take a closer look at the Bayeux Tapestry during a media preview ahead of the official opening at the British Museum in central London on September 7, 2026. — AFP pic
Around the country, students who learn about the artwork in history classes are gearing up for school trips, while businesses are bidding to capitalise on some of the fervour.

Dish towels, aprons and mugs featuring scenes from the tapestry are already on sale at the London museum, while luxury store Liberty has released cushions inspired by the artwork, priced at £165 each (RM910).

Even the budget bakery chain Greggs has jumped on the bandwagon, lightheartedly unveiling its own embroidered “Ta-Pastry” to tell the story of “the conquest of the British high street by our most treasured (and tasty) artifacts”.
A museum in Reading, west of London, is enjoying a flurry of attention for its little-known Victorian replica of the tapestry.

And in the heart of the capital, near the British Museum, a pub has hung up an eight-metre embroidered “Beer Tapestry” recounting the history of brewing in a playful tribute to the more violent original.

“I think it’s quite hard to explain to French people the excitement in the UK. I think the French don’t realise what a big treasure they’ve got,” exhibition curator Michael Lewis told AFP during a preview.
“The British are kind of completely crazy about this object because it’s such a fundamentally important object for our history.”
‘Processional experience’

Plans to loan the tapestry to London had been considered twice before, but both were aborted: in 1953 for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II, and in 1966 for the 900th anniversary of the Battle of Hastings.
In what is believed to be its first time travelling outside France, the tapestry depicting 627 figures and more than 700 animals has been laid flat in a raised glass cabinet.
In its home in Bayeux, it is displayed hanging vertically.
Animations projected on the wall accompany the tapestry, zooming in on details and key events and characters in the artwork, which is replete with gore and drama.
“It’s quite a processional experience because people have to go bit by bit through the tapestry,” Lewis said.
Artists and conservators watched nervously as the delicate, 11th-century artwork was transported by truck in a risky operation from its home in northern France to the British capital.
Initially declared a success with “no visible alteration” to the 70-metre-long tapestry following its arrival, France last week said two broken threads were spotted during a full condition check.
However, the British Museum said the embroidery was “virtually unchanged” with thread breaks, measuring a few millimetres at most, not considered significant damage. — AFP
2297ddcb336368a6: VENICE, Sept 11 — A new documentary from two Oscar-winning Israeli filmmakers that promises to shed light on Israel's killing of civilians in Gaza is set to premiere at the Venice Film Festival on Thursday.
NAZA by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor promises fresh revelations about the bombing of Gaza based on testimony from Israeli forces.

“Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” the pair said when they announced the film in August.
It has been produced by British duo Jim Wilson and Jonathan Glazer – the team behind Auschwitz-set Oscar winner The Zone of Interest – as well as Britain’s Guardian newspaper.

The title is taken from an Israeli military acronym used euphemistically by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that are expected to be killed in an airstrike, according to The Guardian.
Israel’s bombardment of Gaza has left around 73,500 Palestinians dead and 174,500 injured since October 2023, according to Gaza’s Hamas-run health ministry.

Along with Palestinians Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, Abraham and Szor shot to fame with their film No Other Land about Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank, which won the Oscar for best documentary in 2025.
NAZA was a late addition to the top competition this year in Venice, where organisers have selected several films about the Gaza conflict as part of the programme.

Citizen Osama about a Gaza photojournalist struggling to find water and food and do his job premiered last week and has since been chosen as the Palestinian entry to compete for best foreign film in the 2027 Academy Awards.
Last year, The Voice of Hind Rajab, a gut-wrenching docu-drama about the killing of a five-year-old Palestinian girl in Gaza by Israeli forces, picked up second prize at the festival.

The films, as well as increasing condemnation of Israel’s conduct in Gaza from top entertainment figures, are part of a broad shift in public opinion in Western countries against the war and Israeli policies.

US actress Susan Sarandon, one of the most persistent critics of the war, claimed this week that the narrative around Gaza and the United States’ financial and military support for Israel had “completely changed”.
“There’s a lot of things that people are aware of now,” the Thelma & Louise star told a news conference.

Sarandon said she was finding it impossible to find work in Hollywood, having been dropped by her agency in 2023 following controversial remarks at a pro-Palestinian rally for which she later apologised.

Israel has consistently denied deliberately targeting civilians in Gaza, blaming militant group Hamas for hiding among the population of the densely packed and besieged enclave where around two million people lived before the war.
Foreign journalists have been prevented from entering and reporting from Gaza since the start of the conflict, other than under tightly controlled conditions with the Israeli military.

The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) says more than 200 Palestinian journalists have been killed in Gaza since October 2023, constituting “the deadliest and most deliberate effort to kill and silence journalists that CPJ has ever documented”. — AFP
79e349492e77a205: PARIS, France, Sept 11 — Girls are at greater risk of dropping out of education when their schools are hit by heatwaves, storms or wildfires linked to climate change, the UN children’s agency said on Thursday.
Unicef analysis suggested that one in 10 or more than 171 million students in 106 countries or territories had their education disrupted by extreme weather last year.
But the agency said girls were worst affected when schools were damaged, classes cancelled or education switched online.
“Girls are at greater risk of dropping out when climate hazards disrupt or close schools,” it said.
“Damage to schools and sanitation facilities, displacement and lost family income can place additional caregiving and water-collection responsibilities on girls.
“These pressures can also increase the risk of child marriage, making it more difficult for girls to return to class when schools reopen.”
According to the analysis, storms were the most common cause of disruption and last year affected 109 million students around the world.
Floods hit at least 70 million while heatwaves disrupted schooling for some 50 million youngsters.
The overall figures for 2025 are down on analysis of the previous year, in which Unicef said nearly 250 million children in 85 countries – one in seven – were affected by climate hazards.
The agency said it had changed its methodology, basing its analysis on information from aid agencies and local media rather than government figures.
Unicef said about one billion or about half the world’s children live in countries at very high risk of climate and environmental shocks.
Lost learning and the effects on literacy and numeracy could lead to lifetime income losses of at least US$200 billion (RM813.8 billion) and worsen global inequalities, it estimated.

Most of the children come from low- and lower-middle income countries “where education systems often lack the resources needed to safeguard learning during climate-related emergencies”, the study said.
Unicef urged governments and their partners to spend more on building new educational facilities to withstand climate and environmental hazards. — AFP
dc076fd74e0ae11d: Kejayaan sesebuah destinasi pelancongan sering dinilai melalui jumlah ketibaan pelawat. Namun, angka yang tinggi tidak semestinya bermaksud pengalaman pelancong turut bertambah baik. Perkembangan terkini di Korea Selatan menunjukkan mengapa kualiti perkhidmatan perlu dinilai seiring pertumbuhan pelancongan.

Data Korea Tourism Organization menunjukkan sebanyak 1,753 aduan pelancong direkodkan antara Januari hingga Julai 2026, melebihi 1,744 aduan sepanjang tahun 2025. Seoul mencatat jumlah tertinggi dengan 665 kes, diikuti Busan sebanyak 594, Incheon 176 dan Jeju 155 kes. Peningkatan ini menarik perhatian kerana ia berlaku ketika Korea Selatan terus menerima jumlah pelancong asing yang tinggi.

Pada pandangan saya sebagai pensyarah dalam bidang pelancongan, angka tersebut tidak boleh terus ditafsirkan sebagai bukti bahawa kualiti pelancongan Korea Selatan sedang merosot. Apabila jumlah pelawat meningkat, bilangan aduan secara mutlak juga berpotensi meningkat. Ukuran yang lebih tepat ialah kadar aduan berbanding jumlah pelancong, contohnya bilangan aduan bagi setiap 100,000 pelawat. Tanpa perbandingan ini, angka aduan sahaja boleh menghasilkan gambaran yang tidak lengkap.

Walaupun begitu, pola aduan tetap memberi isyarat penting tentang tekanan terhadap sistem destinasi. Aduan berkaitan penginapan merupakan kategori terbesar dengan 500 kes, termasuk pembatalan tempahan secara sepihak dan caj pembatalan yang terlalu tinggi. Layanan tidak mesra dan caj berlebihan di premis perniagaan pula mencatat 376 kes. Selain itu, 186 aduan melibatkan lapangan terbang dan syarikat penerbangan, manakala 182 lagi berkaitan pemandu teksi yang enggan menggunakan meter atau memandu secara berbahaya.

Situasi ini menunjukkan bahawa pengalaman pelancong tidak dibentuk oleh satu organisasi sahaja. Hotel yang baik tidak mampu menutup pengalaman buruk dengan pengangkutan, peniaga atau perkhidmatan lain. Pelancong akhirnya menggabungkan semua interaksi tersebut sebagai gambaran terhadap bandar dan negara yang mereka lawati. Oleh itu, kualiti destinasi perlu dilihat sebagai satu rantaian pengalaman yang saling bergantung.

Busan memberikan contoh yang jelas tentang cabaran mengurus lonjakan permintaan. Bandar itu menerima kira-kira 110,000 pengunjung sempena konsert jelajah dunia BTS pada Jun 2026. Acara besar seperti ini membawa manfaat ekonomi, tetapi pada masa yang sama memberi tekanan kepada penginapan, pengangkutan dan tenaga kerja perkhidmatan. Jika kapasiti tidak bersedia, kejayaan menarik pelancong boleh bertukar menjadi ketidakpuasan di lapangan.

Isu penginapan perlu diberi perhatian khusus. Kenaikan harga ketika permintaan tinggi masih boleh berlaku melalui mekanisme pasaran. Namun, terdapat perbezaan antara harga yang tinggi tetapi telus dengan amalan yang menyebabkan pelancong merasakan mereka dieksploitasi. Pembatalan tempahan yang telah disahkan atau caj yang tidak jelas boleh menjejaskan kepercayaan terhadap destinasi. Dalam pelancongan, kehilangan kepercayaan lebih sukar dipulihkan berbanding kehilangan satu transaksi.

Risiko ini menjadi lebih besar dalam persekitaran digital. Pengalaman negatif boleh dikongsi melalui video pendek, ulasan dalam talian dan media sosial dalam masa yang sangat singkat. Satu aduan yang tidak diselesaikan dengan baik boleh mempengaruhi persepsi ribuan bakal pelancong. Sebab itu pengurusan aduan tidak seharusnya dianggap sebagai fungsi khidmat pelanggan semata-mata. Ia juga merupakan sebahagian daripada pengurusan reputasi destinasi.

Aduan sebenarnya ialah sumber data yang bernilai. Jika masalah berulang pada penginapan, pihak berkuasa boleh meneliti pola pembatalan dan harga. Jika isu teksi tertumpu di lokasi tertentu, penguatkuasaan boleh disasarkan dengan lebih tepat. Jika aduan meningkat ketika acara besar, perancangan kapasiti perlu diperbaiki sebelum acara seterusnya. Destinasi yang matang bukan destinasi tanpa aduan, tetapi destinasi yang mampu mengesan pola masalah dan bertindak dengan cepat.

Profil pengadu juga perlu dibaca dengan berhati-hati. Warga China mencatat jumlah aduan tertinggi, diikuti pelancong Jepun dan Taiwan. Namun, angka ini tidak membuktikan bahawa sesuatu kewarganegaraan lebih mudah tidak berpuas hati. Perbandingan hanya bermakna jika jumlah aduan dinilai bersama saiz pasaran dan jumlah ketibaan daripada setiap negara.

Pengalaman Korea Selatan mempunyai pengajaran yang jelas untuk Malaysia, khususnya ketika negara berusaha meningkatkan ketibaan pelancong dan menarik lebih banyak acara antarabangsa. Kempen promosi boleh meningkatkan permintaan dengan cepat, tetapi kapasiti hotel, pengangkutan dan tenaga kerja memerlukan masa untuk disesuaikan. Jika jurang ini terlalu besar, pertumbuhan pelawat boleh menghasilkan tekanan perkhidmatan yang akhirnya menjejaskan imej destinasi.

Malaysia juga perlu melihat data aduan sebagai sebahagian daripada sistem pengurusan destinasi. Petunjuk seperti kadar aduan, jenis isu, lokasi kejadian, tempoh penyelesaian dan kecenderungan pelancong untuk berkunjung semula patut dinilai bersama angka ketibaan dan hasil pelancongan. Pendekatan ini memberikan gambaran yang lebih tepat tentang kesihatan sebenar industri.

Bagi saya, persoalan utama bukan bagaimana sesebuah destinasi boleh menghapuskan semua aduan. Sasaran itu tidak realistik dalam industri yang melibatkan jutaan interaksi manusia. Cabaran sebenar ialah memastikan pertumbuhan pelancongan disokong oleh sistem perkhidmatan yang mampu bertindak apabila kegagalan berlaku. Destinasi yang benar-benar kompetitif bukan sekadar berjaya menarik pelancong, tetapi mampu memberikan pengalaman yang cukup baik untuk membuatkan mereka mahu kembali dan mengesyorkannya kepada orang lain.
Penulis ialah pensyarah Fakulti Pengurusan Hotel dan Pelancongan Universiti Teknologi Mara.
